Results: gini 0.3917350868 vs 0.3917347200 (diff 3.7e-7); top1 0.3473955665 vs 0.3473961209 (5.5e-7); peak 0.4 vs 0.4 (0.0); entropy 1.4917025194 vs 1.4917048831 (2.4e-6); profile max|diff| 8.0e-7; per-layer ranking identical [4,3,5,0,2,1]. result.paper_check: Fetched arXiv abs page + full LaTeX source (e-print) of 2310.10348: title "Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery", authors Syed, Rager, Conmy — matches PAPERS.md/REPOSITORIES.md. main.tex line 155 gives Eq(2): L(x_clean|do(E=e_corr)) ~= L(x_clean) + (e_corr - e_clean)^T dL/de_clean =: Delta_e L; line 159 gives Eq(3) |Delta_e L| (absolute attribution score, used for ranking). BLME's kernel |sum((clean-corr)*grad)| (edge_attribution.py:172-173) equals |Delta_e L| exactly (sign-invariant). Venue claim "BlackboxNLP 2024" confirmed via ACL Anthology 2024.blackboxnlp-1.25; arXiv comments also say NeurIPS 2023 ATTRIB Workshop (both stated in BLME docs/tests).

result.paper_check: Grassberger & Procaccia, "Characterization of Strange Attractors", Phys. Rev. Lett. 50(5):346-349 (1983) — authors/journal/volume/pages confirmed (APS page returned 403; Wikipedia "Correlation dimension" used as alternate primary summary). Defining equations: C(eps)=lim g/N^2 with g=#pairs at distance<eps; C(eps)~eps^nu; nu = log-log slope. BLME computes C(r)=#{i<j: d<r}/(N(N-1)/2) and the log-log polyfit slope: the normalization differs from 1/N^2 only by a constant (intercept-only, slope-invariant) and excludes self-pairs, the standard correction the paper's practice and nolds' [cd_2]/[cd_3] source comment both endorse. Percentile (5-95) radius window is a documented scaling-region choice (module docstring lines 28-30; ledger + fixture record the resulting dim>~1.5 downward bias). Paper predates arXiv; no arXiv id claimed anywhere — correct.
result.official_code_check: No author code exists (1983). De-facto reference nolds.corr_dim compared line-by-line: fetched raw.githubusercontent.com/CSchoel/nolds/master/nolds/measures.py (corr_dim ~lines 2573-2681) AND read the installed copy at /home/dtsaras/miniconda3/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nolds/measures.py. Confirmed: csums = 1/(n(n-1)) * sum(dists<=r); poly_fit(log rvals, log csums, 1); dists initialized np.zeros((n,n)) so the raw API counts n diagonal self-pairs — exactly the upstream artifact BLME's fixture documents (nolds' own comments say self-matches should be excluded per its refs [cd_2]/[cd_3]). BLME (i<j upper triangle, strict <) == artifact-corrected official nolds output to 0.0 on a fresh signal; '<' vs '<=' verified tie-free. BLME is faithful; the raw-API delta is nolds' bug, correctly not inherited.

result.paper_check: arXiv:1906.04341 "What Does BERT Look At? An Analysis of BERT's Attention", Clark, Khandelwal, Levy, Manning — title/authors/arXiv id match BLME docs. Section 3.3 "Focused vs Broad Attention": "we compute the average entropy of each head's attention distribution", plotted in nats (Figure 4). candidates.name: Attention-map topological features (TDA4ATD, Kushnareva et al.)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/danchern97/tda4atd (verified; self-declared official repo for the EMNLP 2021 paper)
candidates.measures: Three interpretable feature families per attention head: (i) topological features of the thresholded attention graph across a threshold filtration — Betti numbers b0/b1, edge count, number of strongly-connected components; (ii) barcode features from Rips persistence on the symmetrized attention-derived distance (H0/H1 bar length, birth/death stats, persistence entropy); (iii) distances of the attention map to template patterns (attention-to-previous-token, CLS, punctuation).
candidates.adds: Fills the single biggest hole in the topology lens: all 5 existing topology_* tasks (homology, betti_curve, persistence_entropy, persistence_landscape, zigzag) consume hidden-state POINT CLOUDS; no BLME task applies filtration-based topology to ATTENTION. interpretability_attention_graph/rollout/entropy/rank compute flow, information and rank statistics, not persistent homology. The features themselves are label-free (the paper's classifier is downstream and not needed); BLME would report per-head/per-layer feature summaries. NEW vs prior survey: not listed there (adopted or rejected) — the survey never evaluated attention-map TDA.
candidates.feasibility: One forward pass with output_attentions=True; per-head graphs are seq_len x seq_len (<=512), so graph stats via networkx and barcodes via CPU ripser are seconds per text; official code uses ripserplusplus (GPU) but the graph/template features are pure numpy/networkx. Deps: networkx, ripser, numpy, transformers. Small-LLM scale trivially tractable with a few hundred texts and head subsampling.
candidates.parity_feasible: Save attention tensors from a pinned BERT/GPT-2 checkpoint on fixed texts; run the repo's feature-extraction code (features_calculation scripts/notebooks) on those exact matrices; pin the per-head feature vectors (Betti counts, SCC counts, barcode stats, template distances) as golden values and assert BLME matches elementwise within float tolerance.

candidates.name: Representation Topology Divergence (RTD)
candidates.venue: ICML 2022 (PMLR v162, Barannikov, Trofimov, Balabin, Burnaev)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/IlyaTrofimov/RTD (verified; official, pip-installable via git, Docker + Colab provided)
candidates.measures: Multi-scale topological dissimilarity between two equal-size point clouds with one-to-one point correspondence, via the R-Cross-Barcode: persistent homology of a comparison graph built from both distance matrices; RTD = sum of barcode lifetimes. For BLME (single model): the adjacent-layer RTD profile across depth, plus mean/max over depth.
candidates.adds: The topological counterpart of the layer-similarity family: geometry_cka / cknna / procrustes_linearity measure linear-kernel, local-kNN, and orthogonal-map alignment; RTD detects multi-scale cluster/loop structure changes that CKA is insensitive to. Distinct from topology_zigzag_persistence, which tracks feature lifespans through union complexes along the whole layer sequence and yields no pairwise divergence score. NEW vs prior survey: not evaluated there (survey covered zigzag from the same group but never RTD).
candidates.feasibility: Deps numpy/scipy/torch; default backend is ripser++ (GPU) but sub-1000-point clouds run in seconds — subsample ~500 tokens with a fixed seed. O(n^2) memory. Fine at small-LLM scale on CPU/one GPU.
candidates.parity_feasible: The rtd package exposes a direct function on two point clouds. Pin golden RTD values by running the official package on (a) fixed synthetic clouds (their notebook examples) and (b) one saved pair of real adjacent-layer activations with a fixed subsample seed; assert BLME's wrapper/reimplementation reproduces the scalar to tolerance.

candidates.name: Euler characteristic curves & profiles (eulearning)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/vadimlebovici/eulearning (verified; official implementation by the paper's authors, MIT license, scikit-learn transformers in descriptors.py)
candidates.measures: Euler characteristic curves (chi of the filtered complex pointwise along a Rips filtration) and 2-parameter Euler characteristic profiles (e.g. distance x codensity), plus Radon/hybrid integral transforms as compact descriptors of the topological signal.
candidates.adds: Fills the explicitly-named 'Euler characteristic' slot in the lens, currently empty. chi(t) is the alternating sum over ALL homology degrees — it carries higher-degree information that the H0/H1-only betti_curve task (single-scale graph read) and homology task (lifespan stats) discard, and it needs no persistence matrix reduction (near-linear cost). The 2-parameter distance-x-density profile is strictly beyond every existing one-parameter topology task and is robust to outliers in a way Rips-only tasks are not. NEW vs prior survey: not listed there.
candidates.feasibility: Core deps numpy + scikit-learn, gudhi for complexes; CPU, very fast (the paper's selling point is meagre computational cost). Token clouds <=2k points per layer are seconds.
candidates.parity_feasible: Run eulearning's ECC/ECP transformers on fixed inputs: their demos/ point clouds plus one saved activation cloud; pin the returned profile vectors and hybrid-transform coefficients as golden arrays; assert BLME output matches elementwise (deterministic, no sampling).

candidates.name: Euclidicity / topological singularity detection (TARDIS)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/aidos-lab/TARDIS (verified; official aidos-lab code for the ICML 2023 paper, BSD-3, pip install . / poetry)
candidates.measures: Per-point Euclidicity score: the multi-scale deviation of local annulus persistent homology from that of a Euclidean ball — quantifying 'manifoldness' and flagging singular points — together with a local intrinsic dimension estimate. Layer-level summary: mean/quantiles/max of Euclidicity over the token point cloud per layer.
candidates.adds: All existing dimension tasks (geometry_intrinsic_dim TwoNN, geometry_lid MLE, geometry_phd_dimension, geometry_correlation_dimension) estimate a dimension while ASSUMING the manifold hypothesis; no task measures where that hypothesis fails. Euclidicity gives an orthogonal signal — singularity/non-manifoldness of the representation space — from the same aidos-lab group whose magnitude work BLME already adopted (geometry_magnitude), but a different quantity. NEW vs prior survey: not evaluated there.
candidates.feasibility: Pure Python on top of ripser-class PH; cost scales with query points x local neighborhoods, so subsample 100-300 query tokens per layer with fixed seed; CPU minutes per layer at small-LLM scale. Python 3.8/3.9 pin in the repo is the main integration nuisance (vendor the core routine, pin numbers against official code).
candidates.parity_feasible: TARDIS ships example point clouds (e.g. pinwheel) and a callable/CLI producing per-point Euclidicity given explicit scale parameters; pin those per-point scores as golden values for fixed clouds and fixed (r, R, s, S) scales, then assert BLME's port matches to tolerance.

candidates.name: Neural persistence (weight-space 0-dim PH)
candidates.venue: ICLR 2019 (Rieck, Togninalli, Bock, Moor, Horn, Gumbsch, Borgwardt)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/BorgwardtLab/Neural-Persistence (verified; official Borgwardt-lab code, Docker-reproducible)
candidates.measures: Per-layer normalized total 0-dimensional persistence of the bipartite weight graph, filtered by normalized |weight| in descending order (union-find over sorted edges); network-level complexity = mean of normalized per-layer scores.
candidates.adds: Would be the ONLY weights-only topological task: every existing topology_* task requires activations, and the weight-space tasks (geometry_weight_norms, geometry_spectral, geometry_mp_bulk_deviation, geometry_schatten) are spectral/norm-based — they say nothing about the CONNECTIVITY structure of large weights that persistence captures. Honest caveat to encode in the task doc: Girrbach et al. (TMLR 2023, arXiv:2307.10865) show NP is dominated by weight variance + spatial concentration for large layers — BLME should report it alongside a variance control (and/or prefer the corrected DGP variant below). NEW vs prior survey: weight-space TOPOLOGY was never surveyed (only weight spectra, judged covered).
candidates.feasibility: Trivially cheap: sort entries of each weight matrix + union-find; no forward pass at all. For transformer d x d matrices either compute exactly (a few seconds each) or per-head blocks. The official repo is TF1-era run via Docker — use it only as the parity oracle on small matrices, implement clean union-find in BLME.
candidates.parity_feasible: Feed small fixed weight matrices (and one real sliced LLM weight block) through the repo's neural-persistence computation inside their Docker image; pin the normalized NP values; assert BLME's union-find implementation reproduces them exactly (deterministic, no tolerance issues beyond float).

candidates.name: Deep graph persistence (corrected neural persistence)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/ExplainableML/Deep-Graph-Persistence (verified; confirmed official code for the TMLR paper)
candidates.measures: H0 persistence of a single filtration over the WHOLE network (all layers standardized and treated as one graph), implicitly capturing persistent paths through the network; fixes the demonstrated caveat that per-layer neural persistence mostly measures weight variance/concentration.
candidates.adds: The methodologically-corrected form of the weight-topology signal: cross-layer persistent paths, which no BLME task touches. If only one weight-topology task is added, prefer DGP as the primary metric with classic NP as a reported sub-score (both parity-pinned); the pair also gives BLME a built-in robustness story (variance-controlled). NEW vs prior survey: not listed.
candidates.feasibility: PyTorch code; depends on the Aleph C++ TDA library for PH (build step) — mitigate by using their code as parity oracle and implementing the union-find equivalent natively. Weights-only, no forward pass; small-LLM scale fine if restricted to per-block subgraphs or downsampled weight matrices with fixed scheme.
candidates.parity_feasible: Run their scripts on small provided/toy MLP checkpoints to pin golden DGP scores for fixed weight tensors; assert the BLME reimplementation matches. Deterministic filtration makes exact matching feasible; the Aleph build is the only friction (Docker it once in CI or pre-pin goldens).

candidates.name: TOHA — topological divergence of attention graphs during generation
candidates.venue: ACL 2026 (accepted; Bazarova et al., incl. Barannikov)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/sb-ai-lab/TOHA (verified; self-declared official repo, run_mtopdiv.py, Docker)
candidates.measures: Per-attention-head Manifold-Topology-Divergence (MTopDiv/cross-barcode) between the prompt-token and generated-response-token portions of the attention graph — a topological 'novelty of response relative to prompt' score whose magnitude in specific heads tracks hallucination.
candidates.adds: Only candidate providing a GENERATION-TIME topological signal (criterion 1 explicitly allows generations): distinct from consistency_self_consistency (sampling agreement over answers) and from all attention tasks (no filtration-based measure). Borderline flag, stated honestly: the paper selects hallucination-aware heads using ~50 annotated samples; a label-free BLME variant must instead report the distribution over all heads (per-layer mean/max/quantiles of MTopDiv), which is computable unsupervised — the repo itself advertises an 'unsupervised TOHA pipeline'. Rank last because of this adaptation and topical overlap with candidate 1 (different computation: cross-barcode divergence vs static graph features).
candidates.feasibility: Requires generation with attention capture (prompt + continuation), then CPU PH on small prompt/response subgraphs; several-times-faster-than-baselines is a paper selling point. Repo is Dockerized with HF deps; core run_mtopdiv.py is plain Python. Tractable at small-LLM scale with short prompts.
candidates.parity_feasible: Decouple from generation for the parity test: save fixed attention matrices with a marked prompt/response split from a pinned model, run the official run_mtopdiv.py on them to pin per-head divergence values, and assert BLME's implementation reproduces them; generation itself is then only upstream data collection under a fixed seed.

findings.suggested_fix: Change docstring line to "predict the NEXT token's identity from the current hidden state".

parity_tests.detail: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=4 pytest tests/tasks/test_reference_parity_formulas.py::test_persistence_entropy_matches_shannon_lifespans tests/tasks/test_topology.py::test_persistence_entropy -q -> 12 passed in 242s (topology test parametrized over mock architectures). Pins fixture [1,1,2]->1.5 AND a live scipy.stats.entropy(base=2) reference at abs=1e-12, importing the real blme _persistence_entropy.

result.fresh_numeric_check: NEW 3-stage check in scratchpad/verify_topology_persistence_entropy/: official giotto-tda 0.6.2 installed in an isolated venv (not the conda env) and run via the public PersistenceEntropy().fit_transform API on 203 fresh cases (200 random lifespan sets n=2..40, a ripser noisy-circle H0 diagram with 24 bars mirroring evaluate()'s kernel path, 2 analytic cases). max|BLME - gtda official| = 2.665e-15; max|BLME - scipy base2| = 2.665e-15; analytic exact: 8 equal bars -> 3.0 (diff 0.0), lifespans [1,3] -> 0.811278124459133 (diff 0.0). None of these inputs are pinned by existing tests. Numeric kernel is fully correct.
result.paper_check: Atienza, Gonzalez-Diaz, Soriano-Trigueros, arXiv:1803.08304 (published Pattern Recognition 107:107509, 2020) Def 3.1 extracted from the PDF: E(A) = -SUM (l_i/L) log(l_i/L) with "log will refer to the log-base-2 function" — exactly BLME's _persistence_entropy (p=arr/total, -sum p*log2 p). BUT the docstring's venue "(Atienza et al., Entropy 2019)" is wrong (dblp confirms no Entropy-2019 paper), and the first docstring citation attaches the Signal Processing 2017 title (arXiv:1512.07613; authors Rucco, Gonzalez-Diaz, Jimenez, Atienza, Cristalli, Concettoni, Ferrante, Merelli) to the wrong author set "Rucco, Castiglione, Merelli et al." (those are the authors of the ECCS-2014 idiotypic-network paper). Metadata's papers string (Rucco 2016; Chintakunta 2015) and REPOSITORIES.md:104 are correct.
result.official_code_check: Official reference per metadata is giotto-tda. Fetched gtda/diagrams/features.py (master): PersistenceEntropy._persistence_entropy (~lines 118-131) computes X_lifespan = X[:,:,1]-X[:,:,0] then scipy.stats.entropy(X_lifespan, base=2) — algorithmically identical to BLME lines 51-58 (scipy auto-normalizes, matching p=arr/total; BLME's p>1e-12 filter equals scipy's 0*log0=0 convention). Also EXECUTED the official gtda 0.6.2 package: agreement 2.7e-15 over 203 cases. Edge conventions: single bar -> 0.0 in both; empty diagram -> BLME 0.0 vs gtda nan/-1.0 fill (guard documented in helper docstring, only reachable for empty H1; not a kernel deviation). Infinite-bar exclusion for pe_h0 and the 2x-max pe_h0_full approximation are explicitly commented internal choices, not claimed as gtda parity.

candidates.name: LapEigvals — Laplacian eigenvalue spectrum of attention maps (label-free feature core)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/graphml-lab-pwr/lapeigvals (fetched; 'Official implementation... accepted at EMNLP 2025')
candidates.measures: Interprets each attention map as a graph adjacency matrix and extracts the top-k eigenvalues of the graph Laplacian per head/layer (plus AttnEigvals/AttnLogDet variants). BLME would register the label-free spectral summaries (spectral gap / algebraic connectivity, top-k eigenvalue profile aggregated over heads and layers), NOT the supervised hallucination probe trained on those features.
candidates.adds: RE-PROPOSAL WITH A GENUINELY NEW ARGUMENT: the prior survey listed this paper (as 'Caspari et al. 2025, attention-map spectral features') as weak/watch SOLELY because the repo was unconfirmed and their downstream use needs labels. Both blockers are now resolved: the official repo exists and the paper is peer-reviewed at EMNLP 2025. Coverage: no existing task computes graph-Laplacian spectra of attention — interpretability_attention_entropy (row entropy), attention_rank/attention_effective_rank (singular values of A itself), attention_rollout (multiplied maps), attention_graph (PageRank/BOS-sink/Gini) are all different operators; the Laplacian spectrum captures connectivity/community structure none of them do.
candidates.feasibility: Forward passes only (attention weights from one pass); eigendecomposition of n_tokens x n_tokens Laplacians on CPU. Repo is Python 3.12/uv, HF transformers; heavy VRAM only for their 7B+ probe experiments — the feature extraction itself runs on small LLMs trivially.
candidates.parity_feasible: Pin a model (e.g., Llama-3.2-1B) + fixed prompts; run their attention-feature extraction stage (DVC pipeline step that computes LapEigvals features) and assert BLME reproduces the per-layer top-k Laplacian eigenvalues to ~1e-6, same normalization (their code defines the exact Laplacian construction for causal/row-stochastic attention).

candidates.name: Under-trained ('glitch') token detection from embedding geometry (Magikarp)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/cohere-ai/magikarp (fetched; official, ~190 stars, per-model verification reports in results/)
candidates.measures: Weight-only indicators of under-trained tokens: (un)embedding-matrix geometry per vocabulary item — e.g., cosine distance of each unembedding row to the mean 'un-trained token' direction after removing the first principal/mean component, input-embedding norms — yielding a ranked under-trained-token score and a model-level scalar: fraction of vocabulary flagged as under-trained / indicator distribution quantiles.
candidates.adds: A vocabulary-space pathology axis BLME entirely lacks: geometry_tokenizer_efficiency measures fertility (tokenizer only), geometry_unembedding measures effective rank/alignment of W_U — neither detects per-token training-coverage failures (SolidGoldMagikarp-class tokens). It is embedding-space anisotropy analysis put to a concrete reliability use; needs no forward passes at all (pure weights), the most label-light method in this batch.
candidates.feasibility: Trivial: reads embedding + unembedding matrices; minutes on CPU for any small LLM. Deps: transformers, Poetry-managed package. Note tied-embedding models need the paper's tied-variant indicator (repo handles this).
candidates.parity_feasible: Run the magikarp pipeline on a pinned model already in their results/ directory (they publish per-model reports) and assert BLME's indicator values and top-N candidate token IDs match the repo's report/output exactly; deterministic weights-only computation makes exact numeric parity achievable.

candidates.name: Transformer block coupling (Jacobian singular-vector alignment across depth/tokens)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/sugolov/coupling (fetched; 'Code release for Transformer Block Coupling... in ICLR2025'; pip-installable, run_coupling_hf / coupling_from_hooks + Colab demo)
candidates.measures: Linearizes each transformer block along token trajectories via its Jacobian, then measures coupling: how well the top-K singular vectors of one block's Jacobian diagonalize another's (norm of off-diagonal residual), aggregated across depth pairs and tokens. Coupling strength emerges with training and correlates with Open-LLM-Leaderboard performance more strongly than parameter count or depth.
candidates.adds: First derivative-level spectral-geometry task: geometry_procrustes_linearity measures orthogonal approximability of hidden STATES, geometry_cka/cknna measure state similarity, geometry_lipschitz measures sensitivity norms — nothing in the 82 examines singular-vector alignment of block JACOBIANS, i.e., whether layers implement spectrally coordinated linear maps. Distinct RMT/spectral signal with a published capability correlation.
candidates.feasibility: Needs autograd Jacobians of blocks w.r.t. hidden states (backward passes, like existing dynamics_sharpness/gradient_flow tasks) — d x d per token per block, so subsample tokens/blocks; authors demo it on quantized HF LLMs in Colab, small-LLM scale fine. Deps: torch, transformers, bitsandbytes optional.
candidates.parity_feasible: Their package is importable: compute coupling on a pinned tiny model (e.g., gpt2/Pythia-160m) + fixed prompt with run_coupling_hf, then assert BLME's independent implementation reproduces the pairwise coupling matrix/aggregate score to float tolerance (deterministic given fp32 and fixed K).

candidates.name: Density-peaks representation landscape (ADP clustering of hidden states)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/diegodoimo/geometry_icl_finetuning (fetched; official NeurIPS 2024 code) + maintained pip package dadapy (sissa-data-science/DADApy, Patterns 2022) implementing the ADP estimator
candidates.measures: Advanced Density Peaks (ADP) clustering of token/prompt hidden states per layer, using dadapy: number of density peaks per layer, peak saddle-point densities and dendrogram/hierarchy, cluster core sizes — a layer-resolved 'probability landscape topography' profile. Label-free core: peak counts and hierarchy statistics (their ARI-vs-subject analysis uses labels and would be excluded).
candidates.adds: BLME has no density-based cluster-structure task at all: geometry_categories is label-defined category coherence, topology tasks (betti/homology) capture holes not probability modes, geometry_intrinsic_dim captures dimension not multimodality. The multimodality/hierarchy of the representation density is an orthogonal geometry axis shown to sharply distinguish ICL vs SFT processing phases across layers.
candidates.feasibility: Forward passes only; ADP is kNN-based, CPU, needs token subsampling to ~1-2k points per layer (dadapy is optimized for this). Deps: dadapy (pip), torch/transformers for extraction. Their full pipeline used A100 for Llama-3-8B but small LLMs are cheap.
candidates.parity_feasible: Two-level pinning: (1) unit parity vs dadapy directly — fixed point cloud in, assert identical cluster count/assignments/saddle densities (dadapy is the official ADP implementation by the method's authors); (2) pipeline parity vs their repo's cluster-computation script on pinned representations with fixed Z threshold and k.

candidates.name: Categorical/hierarchical concept geometry in the unembedding space (causal inner product)
candidates.venue: ICLR 2025 oral; Best Paper at ICML 2024 Mech-Interp Workshop (Park, Choe, Jiang, Veitch)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/KihoPark/LLM_Categorical_Hierarchical_Representations (fetched; official, 7 numbered validation notebooks, WordNet extraction scripts included)
candidates.measures: Under the causal inner product (unembedding whitened by its covariance), tests whether (a) categorical concepts form regular simplices/polytopes of their element vectors and (b) hierarchical parent-child relations are encoded as orthogonality of concept-difference vectors. Scalars: mean hierarchy-orthogonality score over ~900 WordNet concepts, polytope-regularity statistics per layer/model.
candidates.adds: A concept-structure geometry axis distinct from anything registered: geometry_unembedding is effective rank of W_U only; repe_concept_separability measures binary concept separation in hidden states; geometry_categories is BLME-custom coherence. None tests hierarchy-as-orthogonality or simplex structure under the causal (whitened) metric — the paper's core, award-winning claim. Uses WordNet word lists, the same label-light lexical-resource standard as consistency_bias_weat's WEAT lists; no benchmark labels, no training.
candidates.feasibility: Light: unembedding matrix + optional single forward passes for context vectors; whitening is one d x d covariance inverse-sqrt. Deps: transformers, nltk (WordNet), scikit-learn. Runs on Gemma-2B/LLaMA-3-8B in the repo; small-LLM fine.
candidates.parity_feasible: Run their notebooks 1-3 on pinned Gemma-2B with the repo's shipped WordNet concept sets, export the per-concept orthogonality/simplex statistics, and assert BLME reproduces them to float tolerance; concept word lists are versioned in the repo so the computation is fully deterministic.

candidates.name: Super weights / super activations (single-parameter criticality)
candidates.venue: arXiv 2024 (rev. 2025), Apple + Notre Dame (Yu, Wang, Shan, Reed, Wan); well-cited in the quantization/outlier literature (not yet a main-venue paper — weakest venue in this batch)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/mengxiayu/LLMSuperWeight (fetched; official — analyze.py, evaluate.py, reproduction scripts for OLMo/Mistral/Phi-3/Llama)
candidates.measures: Data-free identification of 'super weights' — single mlp.down_proj parameters whose removal raises perplexity by ~3 orders of magnitude — by locating coincident input/output activation spikes in ONE forward pass; plus the linked 'super activation'. Model-level scalars: super-weight count, magnitude ratio vs layer median, and perplexity-ratio-on-zeroing sensitivity.
candidates.adds: Weight-space outlier CONCENTRATION, which the activation-side tasks do not capture: interpretability_activation_sinks measures massive activations/sink fractions and interpretability_activation_kurtosis measures distribution tail shape, but neither localizes criticality to individual parameters nor quantifies the single-point-of-failure structure that predicts quantization fragility. Flag honestly: closest-to-covered candidate in this batch (same phenomenon family as Sun 2024 massive activations); include only if the committee accepts 'weight-space localization + causal criticality' as a distinct signal.
candidates.adds_overlap_note: moderate overlap risk with activation_sinks family — reviewed and flagged
candidates.feasibility: Trivial: one forward pass with hooks on down_proj inputs/outputs; perplexity check for the sensitivity scalar uses existing BLME perplexity machinery. CPU/small-GPU fine for 1-7B models.
candidates.parity_feasible: The paper publishes an index of super-weight coordinates for public LLMs and the repo has detection scripts: assert BLME's detector returns exactly the published (layer, row, column) coordinates for pinned models (e.g., Llama-7B, Mistral-7B, OLMo-1B) and matching activation magnitudes from the repo's analyze.py output.

candidates.name: Local Learning Coefficient (LLC) via devinterp
candidates.venue: arXiv 2023 (rev. 2024), Lau, Furman, Wang, Murfet, Wei; well-cited foundation of the developmental-interpretability literature; implemented in the maintained devinterp package (v2.0.1, Apr 2026)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/timaeus-research/devinterp (fetched; MIT, pip 'devinterp', supports 85+ HF model types incl. Qwen2.5-0.5B example)
candidates.measures: Singularity-aware effective complexity of the trained network: the local learning coefficient (RLCT estimate) of the loss-landscape geometry at the final weights, estimated by SGLD sampling of the self-supervised LM loss on unlabeled text (no benchmark labels). Output: scalar LLC (+ per-component refined LLC variants from arXiv:2410.02984).
candidates.adds: Loss-landscape DEGENERACY, which is provably different from curvature: dynamics_sharpness (Hessian trace/SAM) measures second-order curvature and is blind to the singular directions the LLC counts; no other task touches singular-learning-theory quantities. HONEST CAVEATS: (1) needs backward passes (SGLD), acceptable only under the same exemption as dynamics_sharpness/gradient_flow; (2) the estimator is hyperparameter-sensitive (step size, localization gamma, chain count), so it is a seeded-pipeline task, not closed-form; (3) no main-venue acceptance verified on the arXiv page. Rank last if criterion 5 ('forward passes only') is enforced strictly.
candidates.feasibility: Gradient-based: ~100s of SGLD steps x a few chains on a small LLM; devinterp's own example runs Qwen2.5-0.5B on a single GPU. Deps: devinterp (pip), torch, datasets, xarray/zarr.
candidates.parity_feasible: devinterp IS the official implementation: BLME would wrap it (like sae-lens is wrapped for interpretability_sae_features) rather than reimplement, pinning devinterp version, seeds, and their documented example config; parity test = fixed-seed LLC on a tiny model reproduces devinterp's tutorial notebook value to tolerance across runs.

result.reasoning: Verified: ablation.py:149-152 uses int(k_pct*100); Python confirms 0.29*100=28.999999999999996 -> "loss_ablate_28pct", and 0.145/0.149 both -> "14pct" (second overwrites first's 4 keys). Defaults [0.01,0.05,0.1,0.25] map exactly; degradation_curve (line 153) and AUC (line 162) unaffected. Cited papers/docstring don't define key naming, so no documented-proxy defense. Real bug, but non-default-config-only mislabeling/collision with correct summary metrics -> low severity.

Reproduced end-to-end on distilgpt2. int(0.29*100)=int(28.999999999999996)=28 → key "loss_ablate_28pct" (mislabel). With config [0.145,0.149,0.29], only 2 loss_ablate_* keys emitted for 3 pcts; combined loss_ablate_14pct=5.8836658 equals the 0.149-alone value, while 0.145-alone (7.9103527) is silently overwritten. Defaults [0.01,0.05,0.1,0.25] map cleanly to 1/5/10/25; degradation_curve/AUC unaffected (AUC=0.11525). Claim confirmed exactly as stated at ablation.py:149-152.

Confirmed. result.paper_check: arXiv:2310.01405 confirmed = Zou, Phan, Chen, Campbell, Guo et al. 2023, "Representation Engineering: A Top-Down Approach to AI Transparency" (matches docs/PAPERS.md:95). arXiv:2308.10248 confirmed = Turner, Thiergart, Leech, Udell, Vazquez, Mini, MacDiarmid 2023, "Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering" (ActAdd); abstract confirms steering vector = contrastive-pair activation difference added during the forward pass — exactly the mechanism BLME implements (mean(h_pos)-mean(h_neg) at last token, added with coefficient alpha). Task metadata cites "Zou et al. 2023; Turner et al. 2023" — both correct. The KL-based effectiveness/success-rate metric is BLME's own, honestly labeled proxy-only.
result.official_code_check: andyzoujm/representation-engineering repe/rep_control_reading_vec.py WrappedBlock.forward: default operator 'linear_comb' -> `current + controller`, applied at token_pos (supports "end" = last token). BLME's hook (representation_engineering.py:348-366) adds (alpha*vec).to(dtype) at [:, -1, :] of the layer output — same mechanism as official linear_comb with token_pos="end". Reading-vector extraction (difference of class means at last token, hidden_states[l+1]) matches the RepE mean-difference reader and ActAdd contrast pair. The KL-divergence effectiveness metric has no official counterpart (proxy, as labeled).

findings.title: Task can never produce metrics in the default pipeline: bundled-pair fallback is unreachable
findings.evidence: Fallback triggers only on `dataset is None`, but core.py:146-148 substitutes the WikiText {"text":...} corpus before tasks run (core.py:285). Empirically: evaluate(model, tok, [{"text":...}]) returns {'error': "Dataset must contain 'text_pos' and 'text_neg' keys."}. Study feature_matrix.csv has 0 steering columns; siblings repe_task_vectors:68-80, concept_separability:178, refusal_direction:494 all fall back on content.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror repe_task_vectors: if the first num_samples items lack text_pos/text_neg, substitute the bundled contrastive triples (lines 283-287) instead of erroring; keep the error only for explicitly malformed user datasets.

findings.title: In-place mutation of the caller's shared dataset dicts (adds 'neutral' key), even on the error path
findings.evidence: `samples = list(dataset)[:num_samples]` copies the list, not dicts; s["neutral"]=... writes into the shared corpus core passes to every task (core.py:285). Verified: corpus[0] became {'text':..., 'neutral': 'The weather today is'} after an erroring evaluate(). Violates the module's own no-mutation invariant (lines 161-171 comment). No current task reads 'neutral', so no numeric impact today.
findings.suggested_fix: samples = [dict(s) for s in list(dataset)[:num_samples]] before mutating. Also delete dead code: `required` set (line 293) and `base_log_probs` (line 343) are never used.

findings.title: No test exercises the default-corpus path, so the dead-in-default-pipeline behavior went unnoticed by two campaigns
findings.evidence: Every test feeds a well-formed {text_pos,text_neg,neutral} dataset; none evaluates the task with the {"text":...} corpus that core.evaluate_model actually passes (core.py:146-148,285). Result: the always-error default behavior and the corpus mutation were invisible while all 56 tests pass. The formula-level parity coverage itself is strong (real blme import, independent fp64 reference).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that runs SteeringEffectivenessTask on a text-only corpus and asserts (post-fix) metrics are produced and the input dicts are unmodified.

findings.title: Ledger row cross-pairs Turner's arXiv id with Zou's repo
findings.evidence: Row lists arXiv 2308.10248 (Turner et al., ActAdd — official repo montemac/activation_additions per docs/REPOSITORIES.md:125) alongside repo andyzoujm/representation-engineering (which belongs to Zou 2310.01405, PAPERS.md:95). The ids are individually correct works but the pairing is internally inconsistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the arXiv column to 2310.01405 (optionally '+2308.10248') or the repo column to montemac/activation_additions so paper and repo columns refer to the same work.

findings.title: steering_success_rate documented as 'fraction of layers' but is fraction of <=5 sampled layers on deep models, and is never emitted in the default flow
findings.evidence: Code tests only layers {0, n/4, n/2, 3n/4, n-1} when num_layers>10 (representation_engineering.py:329-333), so the denominator is 5, not all layers; doc says 'Fraction of layers'. Also the doc presents the feature as produced, yet the default pipeline always errors (finding 1) — 0 steering columns in the study's feature_matrix.csv.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the 5-layer depth subsample (or emit tested-layer indices), and note the dataset requirement until the fallback fix lands.

result.reasoning: Reproduced through the real task: with o_proj in_features=100, num_heads=12, config.head_dim=None, evaluate() crashes at attention_knockout.py:176 with "TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'" — getattr at line 173 returns the existing None instead of the 100//12 fallback. Controls: head_dim attribute absent → runs clean; divisible in_features=96 → runs clean. Severity as claimed: unreachable on standard architectures (o_proj width = num_heads*head_dim), crash-robustness only.

result.summary: The model layer (src/blme/models/wrapper.py, src/blme/utils.py) is small and mostly sound for the gpt2-class happy path, but has three MAJOR release blockers verified by execution: (1) a missing/typo'd `pretrained` key silently evaluates gpt2 instead of the intended model; (2) the documented `load_in_8bit`/`load_in_4bit` args are broken on transformers 5.x, which the unbounded `transformers>=4.35.0` pin installs by default; (3) `device_map=auto` — the docstring's headline usage — crashes on a clean install because `accelerate` is not a declared dependency. Additional minor issues: deprecated `torch_dtype` kwarg warns on every load, the CausalLM→AutoModel fallback masks real load errors behind a pointless retry, seeding omits cudnn determinism and gives task results that depend on which other tasks ran first, and the pad-token fallback can silently leave pad_token=None.

findings.title: Missing or typo'd `pretrained` key silently evaluates gpt2 instead of the requested model
findings.evidence: `args.get("pretrained", "gpt2")` plus parse_model_args dropping non-`k=v` pairs (line 39). Ran `load_model_and_tokenizer('meta-llama/Llama-3-8B')` -> output: `BARE NAME: silently loaded gpt2 GPT2LMHeadModel`. No warning; all downstream results are for the wrong model.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `pretrained` explicitly (raise ValueError if absent) and raise on model_args tokens that lack `=` instead of silently discarding them.

findings.title: Documented `load_in_8bit`/`load_in_4bit` args are broken on transformers 5.x (installed by the unbounded pin)
findings.evidence: Env has transformers 5.2.0 (pyproject pins `transformers>=4.35.0`, no upper bound). Ran `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('distilgpt2', load_in_8bit=True)` -> `TypeError: GPT2LMHeadModel.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'load_in_8bit'`. The kwarg was removed in v5; wrapper docstring (lines 103-104) still advertises it.
findings.suggested_fix: Build a `BitsAndBytesConfig` and pass `quantization_config=` (works on 4.x and 5.x), or add an upper bound `transformers<5` in pyproject and note the limitation.

findings.title: `device_map=auto` (the docstring's headline usage) crashes on a clean install: `accelerate` is not a declared dependency
findings.evidence: pyproject.toml:19-27 dependencies omit `accelerate`; active python lacks it. Ran wrapper with `load_in_8bit=true` (which sets device_map=auto) -> `ValueError: Using a device_map ... requires accelerate. You can install it with pip install accelerate`. Docstring line 8 shows `device_map=auto` as primary CLI usage.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `accelerate` to core dependencies (or an extras group referenced in the docstring), and fail with a clear message when `device_map` is requested without it.

findings.title: Uses deprecated `torch_dtype` kwarg; prints deprecation warning on every model load under transformers 5.x
findings.evidence: Ran `load_model_and_tokenizer('pretrained=gpt2,dtype=float16')` on transformers 5.2.0 -> stderr: `torch_dtype is deprecated! Use dtype instead!`. Load still succeeds (dtype=torch.float16) but will break when transformers removes the alias.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `dtype=` when transformers >= 4.56 (or version-gate: try `dtype`, fall back to `torch_dtype`).

findings.title: CausalLM->AutoModel fallback catches broad ValueError/OSError, masking real load errors and retrying a full second load
findings.evidence: `except (ValueError, OSError)` at wrapper.py:216 logs the root cause only at INFO (`CausalLM failed ({e}), trying AutoModel...`). Verified: the missing-accelerate ValueError triggered a pointless AutoModel retry before finally failing; gated-repo/auth OSErrors would likewise re-download and surface the second error, not the first.
findings.suggested_fix: Only fall back when the error indicates an unrecognized-for-CausalLM config (e.g. match the specific `Unrecognized configuration class` ValueError); re-raise everything else immediately.

findings.title: Determinism gaps: no cudnn/deterministic-algorithms settings, and per-task results depend on which tasks ran before them
findings.evidence: set_global_seed (utils.py:17-28) seeds random/numpy/torch only; no `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic`, `benchmark=False`, or `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms`. core.py:88 calls it once per evaluate(), so a task's RNG stream shifts with the task list; tasks/interpretability/weight_activation_alignment.py:223 already works around this by re-seeding locally.
findings.suggested_fix: Add cudnn determinism flags (optionally behind a flag) to set_global_seed, and re-seed before each task in core.evaluate so task results are independent of the task list.

findings.title: Pad-token fallback can silently set pad_token=None and never sets model.config.pad_token_id
findings.evidence: If a tokenizer has neither eos nor bos, lines 136-137 assign `tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.bos_token` (None) with no warning; later `tokenizer(..., padding=True)` fails with the generic 'tokenizer does not have a padding token'. `model.config.pad_token_id` is never aligned, so generate() warns and tasks patch it ad hoc (generation_diversity.py:185, self_consistency.py:97).
findings.suggested_fix: Raise or add a distinct pad token via add_special_tokens when both eos and bos are missing; set `model.config.pad_token_id = tokenizer.pad_token_id` after load.

result.reasoning: Confirmed: line 173's getattr(model.config,"head_dim",...) returns stored None (default only covers missing attrs); line 176 then raises the exact claimed "TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'" — reproduced through the real task (o_proj in=100, heads=12, head_dim=None). head_dim=None ships in 5 HF configs (mixtral, ministral, minimax, hunyuan x2), but all have o_proj_in=32x128=4096, divisible, so the branch is dead on real models. Real but latent.
result.corrected_severity: low — latent crash-robustness defect on a fallback path unreachable by any standard architecture; no shipped numbers affected

result.reasoning: Confirmed: hidden_states[L]==ln_f(raw block output) (allclose True) while the hook replaces raw output; layers 0-4 match raw exactly (cos=1.0). Last-layer mean mismatch cos=0.316, norm ratio 0.436; importance inflated 4.2667 vs 3.4494 self-consistent (WikiText defaults; fallback corpus 2.8264 vs 2.0036). But the claimed circuit flip [5] vs [1] did NOT reproduce on either default data path — selection stays [1] both ways; only layer_importances and minimality share (0.2386 vs 0.2454) shift. Real bug, impact overstated.
result.corrected_severity: BUG (confirmed, but lower impact than claimed: last-layer importance inflated ~24-41%; no circuit flip at default top_k_pct=25 on either default corpus, so downstream faithfulness/quality shift only marginally)

result.reasoning: Confirmed. transformers 5.2.0 GPT2 appends the last hidden_states entry after ln_f (modeling_gpt2.py:678-683); the hook replaces raw block output. Reproduced on distilgpt2/default corpus: layers 0-4 cos=1.0000; layer 5 cos=0.3160, norm ratio 0.4357; last-layer importance 4.2667 buggy vs 3.4494 self-consistent (~24% inflated), and ln_f is applied twice. Undocumented, so not an honest proxy. But the claimed circuit flip did not reproduce ([1] both ways), so downstream-score corruption is data-dependent.

result.summary: The core loop is largely sound: task registration/discovery works, unknown-task fail-fast happens before model load, per-task exception isolation works, the SIGALRM handler is correctly guarded against non-main-thread use, and all hook-registering tasks remove hooks in try/finally. However, live testing exposed four real gaps: (1) the per-task timeout is one-shot and any broad `except Exception` in task code (57 such handlers exist in blme's own tasks) swallows the TimeoutError, letting the task run unbounded and be reported OK; (2) a task returning a non-dict crashes print_results_table after all tasks ran but before save_results, losing the whole run's results; (3) the shared-cache forward pass is outside error isolation, so one bad dataset sample (e.g. empty text) kills the run before any task executes; (4) cache_num_samples is resolved from task configs after the default corpus is already loaded (capped at 200), so the envelope can record a resolved sample count far larger than what was actually cached — a silent reproducibility hole. Plus several minor envelope/UX defects (summary counts don't add up, list-form YAML tasks crash, fixed output filename overwrites, no inter-task GPU cleanup).

findings.title: Per-task timeout defeated by broad except handlers in task code; task runs unbounded and reports OK
findings.evidence: Live test: task with `timeout: 2` and an inner `except Exception` ran 8s, swallowed the TimeoutError once (alarm never re-fires), and printed "zz_slow_swallow ✓ OK 8.0s swallowed=1". blme's own tasks contain 57 broad excepts (e.g. tasks/common.py:250 `except (TypeError, ValueError, Exception)`), so real tasks can silently outlive their timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Have _timeout_handler set a deadline-expired flag; in the finally block, if the flag is set but no TimeoutError propagated, record the task as timed out and discard its result. Alternatively re-arm the alarm (signal.setitimer with interval) or run tasks in a subprocess for a hard kill.

findings.title: Task returning a non-dict crashes print_results_table after all tasks ran, and results are never saved
findings.evidence: Live test: a task returning None → `"error" in result` raises `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable`; evaluate() aborts between envelope build and save_results, results.json is never written (verified: file absent). One misbehaving task destroys the entire run's output despite all other tasks succeeding.
findings.suggested_fix: In core.py, validate the task's return value when storing (non-dict → route to task_errors); call save_results before print_results_table (or wrap the pretty-print in try/except) so disk output can never be lost to a display bug.

findings.title: Shared-cache forward pass runs outside error isolation; one bad dataset sample kills the whole run
findings.evidence: Live test: dataset containing one `{"text": ""}` entry → cache.populate() raises `RuntimeError: cannot reshape tensor of 0 elements...` and evaluate() aborts before any task runs — no envelope, no partial results. _run_forward_pass (cache.py:350-383) has no per-sample guard, and core.py:251 calls populate() outside the per-task try/except.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip empty/failed samples inside the cache loop with a warning (and keep _sample_lengths consistent), and wrap cache.populate() in core.py in try/except that degrades to cache=None instead of aborting the run.

findings.title: Envelope records cache_num_samples_resolved larger than what was actually cached; default corpus size fixed before resolution
findings.evidence: Live test: geometry_svd num_samples=500 with a 12-sample dataset → log "forward pass over 12 samples", yet envelope reports "cache_num_samples_resolved": 500 with no warning. Default-corpus path has the same bug: corpus is loaded with `cache_num_samples or 200` (core.py:148) before cache_num_samples is resolved from task configs (core.py:231-237), so any task num_samples > 200 is silently capped at 200 while the envelope claims the larger number.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve cache_num_samples from task configs before loading the default corpus; record the actual number of samples cached (len(cache._sample_lengths)) in cache_settings and warn when it is below the requested/resolved count.

findings.title: List-form `tasks:` in a YAML recipe crashes with an unhelpful AttributeError
findings.evidence: Recipe with `tasks:\n  - geometry_svd\n  - geometry_lid` (the most natural YAML style and lm_eval's convention) → `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'keys'` from `list(tasks_dict.keys())`, even under --dry-run. Verified by running run_from_yaml on such a recipe.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept both forms: if the recipe's tasks value is a list, convert to `{name: {} for name in tasks}`; otherwise raise a clear ValueError naming the expected format.

findings.title: Envelope summary counts don't add up: unknown tasks and lm_eval grouping break total = completed + failed
findings.evidence: Live test with 4 requested tasks (1 unknown): summary was {"total_tasks": 4, "completed_tasks": 2, "failed_tasks": 1} — the skipped unknown task is counted in total but nowhere else. lm_eval tasks are also counted individually in total but appear as a single "_lm_eval" entry in completed/failed, so the arithmetic is wrong for any mixed run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a "skipped_tasks" count (unknown tasks) and count lm_eval sub-tasks consistently, so total_tasks == completed + failed + skipped holds in the envelope.

findings.title: save_results silently overwrites previous runs, and CSV output drops errors, metadata, and nested metrics
findings.evidence: Output path is always output_dir/results.json (results.py:197) — two runs into the same output_dir clobber each other with no warning. CSV mode (results.py:203-217) writes only top-level scalar metrics: task errors, all envelope metadata (seed, git hash, configs), and nested per-layer dicts are silently omitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Include a timestamp or model slug in the filename (or refuse/warn on overwrite); for CSV, flatten nested dicts (dotted keys) and emit an accompanying errors/metadata sidecar, or document that CSV is lossy.

findings.title: No GPU/resource cleanup between tasks; empty_cache only runs after an OOM already happened
findings.evidence: The per-task loop (core.py:267-302) never calls torch.cuda.empty_cache()/gc.collect() between tasks; core.py:292 clears the cache only inside the OutOfMemoryError handler. A memory-heavy task's leftover allocations (tensors kept alive by exception tracebacks) can cascade OOMs into subsequent tasks that would otherwise fit, turning one failure into many.
findings.suggested_fix: In the finally block of the task loop, drop the task object, call gc.collect(), and torch.cuda.empty_cache() when on CUDA, so each task starts from a clean allocator state.

findings.title: Fractional per-task timeout silently disables the alarm
findings.evidence: `signal.alarm(int(timeout_sec))` truncates: a recipe `timeout: 0.5` (or any value < 1) becomes alarm(0), which cancels the alarm entirely — the task runs with no timeout and no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `max(1, int(round(timeout_sec)))` or signal.setitimer (which accepts floats), and warn if the configured timeout was coerced.

findings.title: Duplicate task registration silently overwrites the earlier class
findings.evidence: register_task() does `_TASK_REGISTRY[name] = cls` unconditionally — two modules registering the same name (an easy copy-paste mistake for contributors adding tasks) silently shadow each other, with which one wins determined by import order in _register_all_tasks.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise (or at least logger.warning) when name is already present in _TASK_REGISTRY and the class differs.

findings.title: resolve_task_config shallow-copies defaults; nested containers are shared with the module-level cache
findings.evidence: `dict(defaults.get(task_name, {}))` copies only the top level; list/dict values (e.g. `k_values: [10, 50, 100]` in defaults.yaml) are shared objects from _DEFAULTS_CACHE. A task that mutates a nested config value in place pollutes the defaults for every later evaluate() call in the same process. User overrides of nested dicts also replace rather than merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Use copy.deepcopy(defaults.get(task_name, {})) before applying overrides.

result.reasoning: Confirmed from primary sources. Paper 2310.10348 p.3: Eq(2) signed ΔeL = (e_corr−e_clean)^T ∂L/∂e; Eq(3) "|ΔeL| ... the absolute attribution score" used for ranking. Official repo @7124ef8 prune_utils.py: `.sum()` then `if attr_absolute_val: current_result.abs()`. BLME edge_attribution.py:173 `attr = np.abs((diff * grad_h[:T]).sum())` matches both; docstring line 10 alone omits |·|. Code correct, docstring formula imprecise — genuine DOC_GAP, correctly classified.

candidates.name: Min-K%++ (calibrated pretraining-data detection)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/zjysteven/mink-plus-plus (verified: fetched; MIT; includes Loss/zlib/Min-K%/Ref/Neighbor baselines)
candidates.measures: Per-token score z = (log p(x_t) - mu_x) / sigma_x, where mu_x and sigma_x are the mean and std of log p(v|context) over the whole vocabulary at that position; averages the bottom k% of token scores. Detects whether text was a training sample by testing if it forms a local mode of the model's conditional distribution — a calibrated upgrade of Min-K% Prob.
candidates.adds: BLME's consistency_contamination implements original Min-K% (Shi 2023) and consistency_membership_inference is loss-based (Yeom/Carlini). Min-K%++ is the current SOTA reference-free MIA (+6-10 AUROC over Min-K% on WikiMIA) and its vocabulary-normalized z-score is a genuinely different statistic (mode-detection, not raw likelihood). NOT in the prior survey. Cleanest add in the whole lens: logits-only, deterministic, single forward pass.
candidates.feasibility: One forward pass per document; needs full log-softmax over vocab per position (cheap at small-LLM scale). Deps: torch + transformers only. Runtime: seconds per 100 docs on a small GPU.
candidates.parity_feasible: High — official repo is a small pure-function scorer. Pin: run zjysteven/mink-plus-plus scoring on fixed texts with pythia-160m/gpt2, capture per-document Min-K%++ scores, assert BLME kernel matches to 1e-6 on identical token log-softmax inputs (same pattern as the existing consistency_contamination parity test).

candidates.name: SelfCheckGPT (n-gram variant; sampling-based hallucination consistency)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/potsawee/selfcheckgpt (verified: fetched; official; pip install selfcheckgpt)
candidates.measures: Zero-resource hallucination score: sample N stochastic responses to the same prompt, then score each sentence of the greedy response for consistency against the samples. The SelfCheckNgram variant builds an n-gram LM from the samples and scores the target sentence's avg/max negative log-probability — no external model at all, only the subject model's own generations.
candidates.adds: Fills the uncertainty/hallucination-detection gap the prior survey declared 'no must-add' — but that verdict rested on a 'no generation' mold the current criteria explicitly drop (BLME already ships generation-based tasks: consistency_self_consistency, dynamics_generation_diversity, dynamics_coe). SelfCheckGPT was NOT in the prior survey. Distinct from consistency_self_consistency (answer-agreement majority vote) and generation_diversity (Self-BLEU diversity): it produces a factuality-consistency score for a target response, the canonical behavioral-consistency hallucination signal. Restrict to SelfCheckNgram to stay single-model (BERTScore/NLI/MQAG variants need auxiliary models — exclude them).
candidates.feasibility: N~10 sampled generations per prompt + CPU n-gram scoring; pip package with stable API. Deps: selfcheckgpt (reference), torch/transformers. Tractable on small LLMs; generation cost dominates.
candidates.parity_feasible: High — decouple generation from scoring: fix a set of pre-generated samples + target sentences, run the official SelfCheckNgram class on them, and assert BLME's reimplementation reproduces avg_neg_logprob / max_neg_logprob exactly (deterministic given fixed inputs; no sampling in the scoring kernel).

candidates.name: POSIX (Prompt Sensitivity Index)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/kowndinya-renduchintala/POSIX (verified: fetched; official; pip install prompt-sensitivity-index)
candidates.measures: For a set of intent-preserving prompt variants (paraphrases, template changes, spelling perturbations), POSIX = mean relative change in log-likelihood of a given response when its prompt is swapped for another variant. A single label-free scalar indexing prompt-robustness; also decomposes by variation type (template vs paraphrase vs spelling).
candidates.adds: BLME's consistency_format_robustness (Sclar) and consistency_paraphrase are performance-spread / BLME-custom proxies; POSIX is the published, principled, likelihood-based sensitivity index that unifies exactly this axis with official code and a pip package. NOT in the prior survey. No labels needed anywhere in the computation — squarely the prompt-robustness lens.
candidates.feasibility: T^2 teacher-forced forward passes per prompt set of size T (T~5-10) — no sampling required if responses are fixed; runs on gpt2-scale in the official quickstart. Deps: the pip package (reference), torch/transformers.
candidates.parity_feasible: High — the library exposes get_prompt_sensitivity(model, prompt_sets, config) returning the scalar plus a trace object. Pin: run it on gpt2 with fixed prompt sets and fixed responses, assert BLME matches the index to float tolerance; the trace object lets us also pin the per-pair log-likelihood matrix.

candidates.name: Sharded Rank Comparison Test (provable benchmark contamination)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/tatsu-lab/test_set_contamination (verified: fetched; official; includes 8 canonical test sets + contaminated-model challenge)
candidates.measures: Statistical test for dataset-level contamination with exact false-positive guarantees: exploits exchangeability — if the model never saw the benchmark, all orderings of its examples are equally likely; compares log-likelihood of the canonical ordering vs shuffled permutations (sharded rank statistic -> p-value). Needs only sequence log-probs.
candidates.adds: Genuinely different signal from consistency_contamination (Min-K% is per-document likelihood-thresholding): this is a set-level hypothesis test with a p-value and FP guarantee — 'is THIS benchmark in the training set' rather than 'is this string likely memorized'. NOT in the prior survey. Complements Min-K%/Min-K%++ as the third leg of the contamination family (doc score, calibrated doc score, dataset-level test).
candidates.feasibility: Forward passes over (num shards x permutations) orderings of a ~1000-example dataset; each pass is cheap teacher-forcing; deterministic given permutation seed. Repo ships ready-made test files (BoolQ, MMLU, GSM8K, ...) and intentionally-contaminated models for validation. Deps: torch/transformers.
candidates.parity_feasible: High — run the official compute_sharded_comparison_test.py on gpt2 + a shipped dataset file with fixed seeds/shard counts, record the test statistic and p-value, assert BLME reproduces both; the repo's deliberately-contaminated models give a built-in positive control.

candidates.name: INSIDE / EigenScore (internal-state semantic consistency of sampled generations) — RE-PROPOSAL with new argument
candidates.repo: https://github.com/D2I-ai/eigenscore (verified: fetched; official, author-maintained)
candidates.measures: Sample K responses to a prompt; take mid-layer sentence embeddings of each; EigenScore = mean log of the (regularized) covariance-matrix eigenvalues (log-det) of those K embeddings — semantic consistency/divergence measured in the model's own dense embedding space, plus test-time feature clipping to expose overconfident hallucinations.
candidates.adds: EXPLICIT RE-PROPOSAL: the prior survey rejected EigenScore (#9) solely because it 'needs sampling' under the old static-forward mold. The current criteria explicitly allow generations, and BLME already ships generation-based tasks (self_consistency, generation_diversity, coe), so that rejection no longer binds. The single-pass reduction to matrix_entropy noted in the prior survey does NOT cover the actual method: covariance is over K sampled generations' embeddings (behavioral dispersion), not over tokens of one pass. Unlike semantic entropy / KLE (still rightly rejected), it needs NO auxiliary NLI model — strictly single-model. White-box complement to SelfCheckGPT's output-space score.
candidates.feasibility: K~10 samples per prompt + hidden-state extraction (one middle layer, last-token embedding) + eigendecomposition of a KxK Gram — trivial post-processing; generation cost dominates. Deps: torch/transformers.
candidates.parity_feasible: High — freeze K generations and their hidden states, run the official EigenScore + feature-clipping functions from D2I-ai/eigenscore on them, assert BLME matches to 1e-6 (same decoupled-generation pattern BLME already uses for coe parity).

candidates.name: PriDe option-ID prior / MCQ selection-bias (label-free permutation debiasing prior)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/chujiezheng/LLM-MCQ-Bias (verified: fetched; official)
candidates.measures: LLMs' inherent selection bias toward option IDs (A/B/C/D) in multiple-choice formats. PriDe estimates the model's prior over option IDs label-free by permuting option CONTENTS across positions on a few samples and decomposing the observed prediction distribution into prior x content term. BLME task: entropy/imbalance of the PriDe prior + prediction flip-rate under option permutation — both computable with zero ground-truth labels.
candidates.adds: A behavioral-consistency axis nothing in the 82 covers: consistency_position_sensitivity is about context position (lost-in-the-middle), consistency_format_robustness about prompt templates — neither measures answer-choice-ID token bias under content permutation, a dominant known failure mode of MCQ-style evaluation. NOT in the prior survey. Caveat honestly: the paper's headline RStd metric uses recall (labels) — BLME must implement only the label-free PriDe prior-estimation kernel and flip-rate, and say so in the docstring.
candidates.feasibility: c (cyclic) or c! (full) permutations x forward passes per item, c=4 options; a few hundred items suffice for a stable prior. No labels, no sampling. Deps: torch/transformers.
candidates.parity_feasible: Medium-high — the official repo's PriDe implementation computes the prior from option-permuted logit distributions without labels; pin by feeding fixed MCQ items + fixed model (gpt2/pythia) through both codepaths and asserting the estimated prior vector and debiased distributions match to 1e-6. Needs modest extraction work since the repo is experiment-oriented rather than a library.

candidates.name: Generating with Confidence: graph-spectral black-box UQ (EigV / Degree / Eccentricity, Jaccard kernel) — same-class-as-rejected-KLE, with new argument
candidates.repo: https://github.com/zlin7/UQ-NLG (verified: fetched; official)
candidates.measures: Sample M responses; build an MxM similarity matrix; uncertainty = sum of graph-Laplacian eigenvalue deficits (EigV, a continuous 'number of semantic sets'), per-response confidence = degree centrality (Deg) and eccentricity (Ecc) in the similarity graph. With the Jaccard-similarity kernel this is fully single-model (no NLI).
candidates.adds: EXPLICIT DISCLOSURE: prior survey rejected KLE (#10) — same family — for needing 'generation + similarity model'. New argument, two parts: (a) generations are now in-mold; (b) unlike KLE, this paper's Jaccard-kernel variant requires NO auxiliary similarity model, removing the second rejection ground. Distinct from SelfCheckGPT (target-vs-samples factuality score) and INSIDE (embedding-space covariance): it is dispersion structure among the samples themselves in output space, yielding both an uncertainty scalar and per-response confidences. Lowest priority of the three sampling-based adds — take it only if the family is wanted in full.
candidates.feasibility: M~10-20 samples per prompt; Jaccard matrix + eigendecomposition of MxM Laplacian is trivial. Restrict to the Jaccard kernel (NLI kernel would violate single-model). Deps: torch/transformers.
candidates.parity_feasible: High — scoring is deterministic given fixed responses: extract the official EigV/Deg/Ecc functions, feed identical fixed response sets, assert equality to 1e-6. Repo is research-pipeline-shaped (persist-to-disk caching), so parity should target its scoring functions, not the end-to-end script.

candidates.name: LLM-Check (single-pass eigen-analysis hallucination scores: attention-kernel + hidden-state log-det)
candidates.arxiv: none — no arXiv listing; peer-reviewed NeurIPS 2024, verified via https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/95584 and https://openreview.net/pdf?id=LYx4w3CAgy (both fetched/confirmed)
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2024 (Sriramanan, Bharti, Sadasivan, Saha, Kattakinda, Feizi)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/GaurangSriramanan/LLM_Check_Hallucination_Detection (verified: fetched; official)
candidates.measures: Hallucination scores from ONE teacher-forced forward pass over (prompt, response) — no sampling, no databases: (a) Attention Score — eigen-analysis (mean log-determinant) of the self-attention kernel similarity map across response tokens; (b) Hidden Score — log-det eigen-score of the response's hidden-state Gram matrix; paper reports 45x-450x speedups over sampling-based detectors.
candidates.adds: The only verified single-forward-pass hallucination detector with official code — fills the prior survey's gap (a) where the sole single-pass option (attention spectral features, #11) had no confirmed repo. The attention-kernel log-det is NOT covered by interpretability_attention_entropy (Shannon entropy of rows), attention_rank (effective rank), or attention_graph. Implement only the Attention/Hidden eigen scores — its Perplexity and Logit Entropy scores duplicate geometry_perplexity and interpretability_prediction_entropy and must be excluded. Hidden Score is adjacent to geometry_matrix_entropy (flag in docs: per-response, response-token-restricted, hallucination-oriented normalization).
candidates.feasibility: Single forward pass with attention outputs + hidden states retained; eigendecompositions of (response-length)-sized matrices per layer/head — cheap at small-LLM scale. Deps: torch/transformers.
candidates.parity_feasible: High — official repo computes scores from captured attention maps / hidden states via small self-contained functions; pin by extracting them, running both on identical cached activations from pythia/gpt2 on fixed (prompt, response) pairs, asserting 1e-6 agreement per layer and on the aggregate. Slight risk: repo is Llama-oriented, so BLME's model-agnostic hook plumbing needs care to capture identical tensors.

result.reasoning: Confirmed by execution: HF GPT-2 hidden_states[-1] == ln_f(block_out) (True), so circuit_quality.py:113's hs[l+1] last-layer mean is post-ln_f while the hook replaces the raw block output (pretrained GPT-2: cos 0.427, norms 183 vs 363; claim said 0.303). Test reference transcribes identical `h = hs[l + 1]`, and in the test's config selected_layers=[0], so layer 2 is ablated with the same wrong mean on both sides — parity passes, bug undetectable. Not documented: comment claims "true mean-ablation baseline." WEAK_TEST correct.
