findings.title: NaN layer poisons summary stats: max_auc_layer points at the NaN layer, max_auc/mean_auc become NaN
findings.evidence: Lines 253-255 use np.argmax/np.max/np.mean on layer_aucs that lines 224-228 deliberately fill with NaN (fp16/bf16 deep-layer path per comment at 221-227). Reproduced on real evaluate(): aucs=[1.0, 0.8519, nan] -> max_auc_layer=2, max_auc=nan, mean_auc=nan; correct nanargmax=0, nanmax=1.0.
findings.suggested_fix: Use np.nanargmax/np.nanmax (and nanmean or document mean_auc semantics), with an all-NaN guard returning an {'error': ...} dict.

findings.title: String-labelled datasets pass the _is_labelled guard then crash at np.bincount
findings.evidence: _is_labelled (172-176) accepts any {'text','label'} dict; label='harmful'/'harmless' (the sibling repe_refusal_direction format, same module) reaches np.bincount(y) at line 214 -> TypeError "Cannot cast array data from dtype('<U8')". Reproduced. Runner's catch-all (core.py:294) contains it, but the task yields no result instead of its own {'error':...} convention.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate labels are binary ints in _is_labelled (or map string labels), returning {'error': ...} otherwise.

findings.title: Task doc claims PCA/LAT reading-vector extraction; code fits a logistic-regression CV probe and computes no reading vector
findings.evidence: Doc says: 'Using Linear Artificial Tomography (LAT) / Principal Component Analysis (PCA)... We determine the principal Reading Vector and measure the accuracy'. Code (rep_eng.py:218-248) uses StratifiedKFold LogisticRegression AUC/acc; no PCA, no reading vector. The parity test itself states BLME measures 'LINEAR SEPARABILITY... not the PCA vector itself'.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword section 2 to: held-out logistic-regression separability probe (AUC/accuracy), a refined adaptation of the paper's linear reading methods (cf. paper section 5.1 LR directions).

findings.title: Parity file tests a transcribed copy of the BLME kernel, not the imported module
findings.evidence: _blme_separability re-implements rep_eng.py:214-248 'verbatim' instead of importing ConceptSeparabilityTask; a formula change in the real module would leave all 5 parity tests green. Compensated by test_comprehensive_parity.py:5905 which runs the real task vs independent cross_val_score (1e-9), so overall coverage is ACCEPTABLE; the NaN-summary path is untested anywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fixture-driven test that calls the real evaluate() via a stub model, including one NaN layer to pin nan-safe summaries.

result.reasoning: Confirmed. Docstring L15/L17 lists "top1_share"/"top1pct_share", but evaluate() returns only "mean_top1_share"/"mean_top1pct_share" (L246-247, plus "mean_top1_saliency_share"/"mean_top1pct_saliency_share" at L240-241); results["top1_share"] would KeyError. The other three documented names (mean_attribution_gini, localization_layer_mean, attribution_layer_entropy) match keys at L245/248/249 exactly. No consumer reads the bare names. Correctly classified as cosmetic DOC_GAP; suggested docstring rename is the right fix.

Reproduced with the test's exact setup. hs[l+1] means are bit-identical to raw block outputs for layers 0-1 but post-ln_f for the last layer (distilgpt2: cos 0.316 vs true mean; claim said 0.303). Test reference matches task faithfulness to 8.4e-10 (passes 1e-5), while a hook-based corrected reference gives 0.9954467 vs task 0.9952480 (diff 1.99e-04 > 1e-5) — would fail, pinning the bug. Last layer is in the ablated non-circuit set, so the test exercises yet misses the bug. WEAK_TEST stands.

Confirmed. tracing.py:41 docstring reads "ROME (Meng et al. 2022, §3.2) uses 3 × σ". In arXiv 2202.05262, §3.2 is "Evaluating ROME: Zero-Shot Relation Extraction (zsRE)" — unrelated to noise. The rule "ν=3σt is set to be three times larger than the observed standard deviation σt of token embeddings" appears in Appendix B.1 (referenced from §2.1 Causal Tracing). Code behavior is correct; only the section citation is wrong. Docstring-only defect.

result.summary: Happy-path determinism holds: two identical `evaluate(model_args="pretrained=distilgpt2", tasks=[4 tasks], seed=42)` runs in fresh processes produced byte-identical results JSON. Most tasks (geometry, causality, topology, repe) correctly use locally seeded generators (np.random.default_rng(seed), torch.Generator().manual_seed(...)), and the results envelope records seed, git hash, and dependency versions. However, seeding is not airtight: ~7 tasks draw from the process-global numpy/torch RNGs that core.evaluate() seeds only once per run, so their feature values silently depend on which tasks ran before them — empirically confirmed (head_roles top-head rankings and scores change when induction_heads runs first; self_consistency's headline metric is 0.375 in a 4-task run vs 0.5 solo). The two sampling-based generation tasks default to seed=None. A few tasks also re-seed the global RNGs mid-run (np.random.seed(42), torch.manual_seed) instead of using local generators, polluting state for downstream tasks and library callers. Docs never mention the --seed flag, the global.seed YAML key, or dtype/device sensitivity despite examples recommending bfloat16.

findings.title: Task feature values depend on run composition: several tasks consume the process-global RNG seeded once per run
findings.evidence: head_roles.py:59 `torch.randint` (no generator); same pattern in induction.py:122, probing.py:82, superposition.py:147, sharpness.py:91. Ran `evaluate(tasks=[head_roles])` vs `evaluate(tasks=[induction_heads, head_roles])`, seed=42, distilgpt2/CPU: mean_duplicate_token_score 0.0803 vs 0.0405; top_previous_token_heads ordering changes (L3H0 vs L1H2 at rank 2).
findings.suggested_fix: Give every stochastic step a local generator derived from the task's config seed (e.g. torch.Generator().manual_seed(cfg_seed + i) / np.random.default_rng(seed)), as already done in geometry/lid.py, causality/ablation.py, and induction.py:248 (which seeds its second half but not its first at line 122).

findings.title: Generation-sampling tasks default to seed=None, so sampled completions ride the global torch RNG
findings.evidence: self_consistency.py:57 `seed = self.config.get("seed", None)` and generation_diversity.py:149 same; defaults.yaml has no seed for either, so do_sample generation uses global RNG. Confirmed: mean_first_token_agreement = 0.375 when run after 3 other tasks vs 0.5 solo (identical seed=42, model, prompts).
findings.suggested_fix: Set a seeded default (e.g. seed: 42 in defaults.yaml for consistency_self_consistency and dynamics_generation_diversity) so the per-prompt torch.Generator path is always taken; keep seed: null as an explicit opt-out for users who want fresh sampling.

findings.title: Tasks re-seed the global RNGs mid-run instead of using local generators (RNG pollution)
findings.evidence: categories.py:145,285,369 call `np.random.seed(42)`; dynamics/stability.py:83 same; self_consistency.py:72 calls `torch.manual_seed(seed)` when a seed is configured. These stomp global RNG state for downstream tasks and for library callers embedding blme. Contrast weight_activation_alignment.py:87-96, which saves/restores torch RNG state around its manual_seed(0).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with local `np.random.default_rng(42)` / `np.random.RandomState(42)` objects (drop the torch.manual_seed in self_consistency; the local torch.Generator at line 74-77 already covers it).

findings.title: Reproducibility knobs and dtype/device sensitivity undocumented
findings.evidence: `grep -rniE 'determinis|reproduc|seed' docs/configuration.md docs/getting_started.md` returns nothing, yet cli.py:85 defines `--seed` and runner.py:38 reads `global.seed` from YAML. Docs examples recommend `dtype=bfloat16` (configuration.md:9,33) with no warning that feature values differ vs float32 or across CPU/GPU (no torch.use_deterministic_algorithms guidance anywhere).
findings.suggested_fix: Document --seed / global.seed in configuration.md, and add a short reproducibility note: same seed+dtype+device+task-list reproduces results; bfloat16/GPU runs are not bit-comparable to float32/CPU runs.

result.reasoning: Reproduced exactly: with unreachable hub, test SKIPPED at line 233 "tiny model unavailable: timed out" despite warm cache (models--hf-internal-testing--tiny-random-gpt2 present with all files). Docstring says "Skips offline if the tiny model isn't cached" — behavior diverges from documented intent. Verified fix: local_files_only=True loads "GPT2LMHeadModel 5 layers" under same endpoint. Lines 235-237 are the file's only blme imports; other 12 tests use transcribed kernel. test_comprehensive_parity.py (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, line 998) covers the real task. WEAK_TEST severity correct.

candidates.name: LLM-as-lossless-compressor (cross-modal arithmetic-coding compression rate)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/google-deepmind/language_modeling_is_compression
candidates.measures: Raw and model-size-adjusted lossless compression rate obtained by driving an arithmetic coder with the model's next-token distribution over raw byte chunks from three modalities: text (enwik8/9), ImageNet grayscale patches, LibriSpeech audio bytes. Compression rate = compressed bits / raw bits per fixed-size chunk.
candidates.adds: The only candidate that measures OUT-OF-MODALITY in-context sequence modeling: geometry_perplexity is text-corpus BPC on tokenized natural language, and never touches image/audio bytes or the adjusted (size-penalized) rate. The cross-modal compression profile (text vs image vs audio) and the adjusted rate are genuinely new capability axes; the paper is the canonical 'prediction=compression' anchor for the eval-without-benchmarks line. Not in the prior survey or skip list.
candidates.feasibility: Forward passes only, logits over ~2048-byte chunks mapped through the tokenizer (their ASCII/byte mapping trick for token-level LLMs). The repo's arithmetic_coder.py is pure-Python and framework-agnostic; JAX is only needed for their in-house trained transformers, not for evaluating HF models. Runtime: a few hundred chunks x 1 forward each — fine for small LLMs on one GPU.
candidates.parity_feasible: Two-stage pin: (1) feed identical probability sequences into their arithmetic_coder.py vs the BLME port and require bit-identical compressed lengths; (2) fix a set of enwik8/ImageNet/LibriSpeech chunks, run their compress_fn wrapped around the same HF model logits, and match compression rates to float tolerance.

candidates.name: Domain-stratified BPC (compression-represents-intelligence protocol)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/hkust-nlp/llm-compression-intelligence
candidates.measures: Sliding-window bits-per-character on three released, dated, contamination-controlled corpora (Common Crawl text, GitHub Python, arXiv math; HF dataset hkust-nlp/llm-compression), with context-window unification (block_size/stride). Shown across 31 LLMs to correlate almost linearly (Pearson ~-0.95) with benchmark 'intelligence' per domain.
candidates.adds: HONEST CAVEAT: the core quantity is BPC, which geometry_perplexity already computes on BLME's own corpus — the add is the flagship eval-without-benchmarks PROTOCOL: the three official domain corpora, the sliding-window/context-unification procedure, and the per-domain BPC profile (code-BPC and math-BPC vs text-BPC ratios) as a capability fingerprint that a single-corpus BPC cannot give. If the parent judges protocol+corpora insufficient novelty, skip; it is the cheapest add on this list.
candidates.feasibility: transformers + datasets only (flash-attn optional); pure teacher-forced forward passes with stride; corpus subsets can be capped for small-model runtime (minutes per domain on one GPU).
candidates.parity_feasible: Run their code/evaluation/main.py (e.g. --task_name cc --block_size 1900 --stride 512) on a small open model over a frozen corpus slice, and require BLME's task to reproduce the per-domain BPC to ~1e-6 with identical block/stride settings.

candidates.name: Text-diversity suite: compression ratio, self-repetition, n-gram diversity, homogenization
candidates.venue: AACL-IJCNLP 2025 system demo (Shaib, Barrow, Sun, Siu, Wallace, Nenkova); widely cited since 2024
candidates.repo: https://github.com/cshaib/diversity
candidates.measures: A standardized battery over a set of model generations: gzip compression ratio of the concatenated outputs (corpus-level redundancy), self-repetition score of long n-grams across outputs, n-gram diversity score, homogenization scores (ROUGE-L/BLEU/BERTScore variants), and syntactic template rate. The paper's comparative analysis recommends reporting the low-mutual-correlation combo: compression ratio + long n-gram self-repetition + Self-BLEU.
candidates.adds: dynamics_generation_diversity covers only Distinct-n and Self-BLEU per prompt. This adds the compression-based diversity family (gzip ratio — an entirely different, information-theoretic signal than n-gram counting), long n-gram self-repetition, and syntactic templatedness. Distinct from geometry_tokenizer_efficiency's compression_ratio (tokens/char, a tokenizer property, no generations involved). Maintained pip package `diversity` (Apache-2.0).
candidates.feasibility: Trivial: reuse the completions already sampled by dynamics_generation_diversity; core recommended metrics need only numpy/nltk/scikit-learn (no external models); BERTScore homogenization and POS templates are optional extras (sentence-transformers/spaCy) we can omit.
candidates.parity_feasible: Deterministic string-in/score-out functions: freeze a set of generation strings, call compression_ratio / self_repetition_score / ngram_diversity_score from the pip package, and require exact (or float-tolerance) equality with the BLME implementation.

candidates.name: MAUVE (divergence-frontier gap between model text and human text)
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2021, Outstanding Paper Award (Pillutla et al.)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/krishnap25/mauve
candidates.measures: Area under the KL-divergence frontier between the distribution of model generations and a human-text reference distribution, computed in a quantized (k-means over embeddings) feature space; summarizes both type-I (model puts mass off human support) and type-II (model misses human modes) errors in one scalar in (0,1].
candidates.adds: A genuine portfolio gap: every existing generation task measures INTERNAL diversity/consistency of the model's own outputs; nothing measures distributional human-likeness of open-ended generation. Needs only an unlabeled human corpus (BLME already ships eval corpora — not benchmark labels). Single-model purity is preservable because compute_mauve accepts precomputed features, so the evaluated model's own hidden states can serve as the embedder (default GPT-2 featurizer also available for cross-model comparability).
candidates.feasibility: pip `mauve-text` (numpy, scikit-learn, faiss-cpu); cost = generating ~500-1000 completions + one featurization pass; k-means on a few thousand vectors is seconds on CPU. Fine at small-LLM scale.
candidates.parity_feasible: Fix generations, reference texts, featurizer, num_buckets, and seed; run compute_mauve from the official package vs the BLME task and require matching MAUVE values (deterministic given seed; also pin the frontier integral on precomputed p_features/q_features arrays).

candidates.name: GRIDE scale-resolved intrinsic dimension + high-dimensional abstraction-phase onset
candidates.venue: ICLR 2025 (Cheng, Doimo, Kervadec, Macocco, Yu, Laio, Baroni); GRIDE estimator: Denti et al., Scientific Reports 2022; DADApy package paper: Patterns 2022
candidates.repo: https://github.com/chengemily1/id-llm-abstraction (paper code; uses https://github.com/sissa-data-science/DADApy, pip `dadapy`)
candidates.measures: Per-layer GRIDE intrinsic dimension of last-token hidden states at geometrically increasing neighborhood scales (2^1..2^13), yielding a scale-resolved ID profile per layer; summary scalars = peak ID and the relative depth of the ID-peak onset ('abstraction phase'), whose earlier onset predicts better LM quality. Paper code also computes information imbalance between layers (asymmetric, rank-based neighborhood predictability).
candidates.adds: All five existing ID tasks are single-scale or global: intrinsic_dim (TwoNN, smallest scale only), lid (fixed-k MLE), phd_dimension (global topological), correlation_dimension (global fractal), magnitude (metric-space size). GRIDE adds the scale axis without subsample decimation, and the abstraction-phase onset depth is a validated LLM-quality predictor no current task emits. Information imbalance additionally offers an ASYMMETRIC layer-comparison signal — cka/cknna/rsa/hsic are all symmetric. New argument beyond prior survey: the survey's 'modern ID' gap was filled with PHD/magnitude but never evaluated a scale-resolved likelihood-ratio estimator; this one comes with an ICLR-2025 LLM-specific validation and a maintained pip dependency.
candidates.feasibility: Forward passes to collect ~5-10k last-token vectors, then CPU-only dadapy calls (minutes). dadapy is maintained (SISSA) and pip-installable.
candidates.parity_feasible: Freeze a point cloud (saved hidden states), run dadapy IdEstimation.return_id_scaling_gride vs the BLME task and require float-tolerance equality across all scales; cross-check the layer profile against the paper repo's dadapy_id.py script on its released 20-token corpora.

candidates.name: Entropy calibration gap (generation entropy-rate drift vs log loss on human text)
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2025 (Cao, Valiant, Liang); classic anchor: Braverman et al., ICML 2020, arXiv:1906.05664
candidates.repo: https://github.com/stevenxcao/entropy-calibration
candidates.measures: Whether the model's per-step entropy over its OWN generations matches its log loss on human text: the miscalibration gap EntRate(generations) - CE(human text), plus the fitted scaling exponent of entropy drift as generation length grows (error-accumulation rate). Computed from sampled continuations + teacher-forced scoring of both the generations and a human corpus.
candidates.adds: A distinct information-theoretic axis: dynamics_generation_diversity's entropy-collapse submetric only tracks the within-generation softmax-entropy trend; consistency_calibration is label-based confidence calibration. Nothing in the portfolio compares the model's generative entropy rate to its predictive log loss — the canonical open-ended degeneration/error-accumulation diagnostic, now with a NeurIPS 2025 measurement protocol and MIT-licensed official code. No benchmark labels needed (raw human text only).
candidates.feasibility: Sampling N continuations per prompt at temperature 1 + forward passes for entropies; their repo uses transformers (vllm optional — skippable for small models). Runtime dominated by generation, comparable to existing generation-based BLME tasks.
candidates.parity_feasible: Freeze prompts and generated token sequences (seeded), then run their entropy-computation scripts (submit_ents_jobs.sh path) vs the BLME implementation on identical sequences; per-step entropies and log losses are deterministic given logits, so require float-tolerance equality of the gap and the fitted drift exponent.

candidates.name: Per-input vs across-input diversity decomposition (EAD / sentence-BERT / NLI diversity)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/facebookresearch/rlfh-gen-div
candidates.measures: Output diversity decomposed into per-input diversity (across N samples for one prompt) and across-input diversity (whether the model produces similar text regardless of prompt), each instantiated with expectation-adjusted distinct n-grams (EAD, corrects distinct-n's length bias), sentence-embedding cosine diversity, and NLI-based semantic diversity. Famous for quantifying RLHF's diversity collapse.
candidates.adds: dynamics_generation_diversity is strictly per-prompt; the ACROSS-INPUT homogenization axis (mode collapse across different prompts, the signature RLHF effect) is not measured anywhere in the portfolio, and EAD is the principled fix to the distinct-n length bias BLME's docstring itself cites. Caveats stated honestly: repo is archived (read-only, but official and complete — diversity/ folder has ead_averaged_distinct_ngrams, sent_bert_from_sim, nli_sample_from_sim) and the SBERT/NLI variants need small external helper models; the EAD variant is dependency-free. Rank this last; adopt at least the EAD per/across-input pair.
candidates.feasibility: Reuses completions from the existing diversity task across BLME's prompt set; EAD is pure counting (no deps); SBERT/NLI variants pull small HF models (optional, ~100M params). CPU-light.
candidates.parity_feasible: Vendor their diversity/ metric functions (MIT-licensed sub-component diversity-eval) as the reference; freeze completion sets and require exact equality for EAD counts and float-tolerance for similarity-matrix-based scores with pinned helper-model versions.

candidates.name: Retrieval heads (retrieval-score head taxonomy)
candidates.venue: ICLR 2025 (confirmed in ICLR 2025 proceedings PDF); Wu, Wang, Xiao, Peng, Fu
candidates.repo: https://github.com/nightdessert/Retrieval_Head (verified: fetched; official, 241 stars; entry point retrieval_head_detection.py -> per-head head_score JSON; supports Llama/Qwen/Mistral/Phi)
candidates.measures: Per-head 'retrieval score': the frequency with which a head attends to and copies the exact needle token it is currently emitting during needle-in-a-haystack greedy decoding. Model-level scalars: fraction of retrieval heads (score>0.1), sparsity/concentration of the retrieval-head set, mean top-k retrieval score.
candidates.adds: New head-taxonomy class absent from interpretability_head_roles (previous-token / duplicate-token / induction are short-range synthetic scores; none measures cross-context copy-during-decode, the documented mechanism behind long-context factuality). Fully label-light: needle+haystack are synthesized, detection is attention-argmax matching, no benchmark labels. Uses generation, which criterion 1 explicitly allows.
candidates.feasibility: torch+transformers only for the algorithm (repo pins flash-attn for caching but detection uses eager attention to expose maps). At small-LLM scale run with 1-4k-token haystacks instead of 50k; deterministic given fixed needle placements. Runtime: minutes per model on 1 GPU.
candidates.parity_feasible: Run the official retrieval_head_detection.py on a small supported model (e.g. Llama-3.2-1B or Mistral-7B at short context) with fixed needle positions/seeds; pin the emitted head_score JSON and require BLME per-head scores to match exactly (the score is a deterministic count ratio).

candidates.name: Norm-based attention analysis (||alpha f(x)|| value-weighted attention)
candidates.venue: EMNLP 2020 (Kobayashi, Kuribayashi, Yokoi, Inui); follow-ups EMNLP 2021 (residual+LN mixing) and ICLR 2024 Spotlight (FF blocks) in the same repo; ~700+ citations
candidates.repo: https://github.com/gorokoba560/norm-analysis-of-transformer (verified: fetched; official, covers all three papers, per-paper directories with notebooks)
candidates.measures: Attention analyzed as the norm of the transformed value vector times the weight, ||alpha_ij f(x_j)||, instead of raw alpha. Scalars: norm-based attention entropy per head, raw-vs-norm attention mass ratio to BOS/special/punctuation tokens (quantifies how much 'sink' attention is actually dead weight), norm-based context-mixing ratio through residual+LN (EMNLP 2021 extension).
candidates.adds: Every existing BLME attention statistic (attention_entropy, attention_rollout, attention_graph, positional_decay, activation_sinks' attention side) is raw-weight based. This is the canonical, heavily cited correction showing raw alpha systematically overweights special tokens — it upgrades a whole task family and directly complements interpretability_activation_sinks by separating 'attention sink' from 'value-norm-cancelled sink'. Single forward pass, weights+activations only, no labels.
candidates.feasibility: Pure torch: needs per-head value vectors and output projection, one forward pass; trivial at small-LLM scale (same cost as attention_entropy). No extra dependencies.
candidates.parity_feasible: The official EMNLP 2020 notebooks compute exact ||alpha f(x)|| matrices for BERT on fixed inputs; pin those tensors and require elementwise match from the BLME kernel (closed-form, deterministic — same parity pattern as the existing attention_rollout test).

candidates.name: Categorical & hierarchical concept geometry (causal-inner-product simplex/orthogonality scores)
candidates.venue: ICLR 2025 Oral + Best Paper at ICML 2024 Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop (Park, Choe, Jiang, Veitch)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/KihoPark/LLM_Categorical_Hierarchical_Representations (verified: fetched; official; numbered notebooks 01-07 computing concept vectors, orthogonality tests, polytope validation on Gemma-2B and LLaMA-3-8B)
candidates.measures: Concept directions in unembedding space under the 'causal inner product' (whitening by the unembedding covariance). Scalars: (a) hierarchy-orthogonality score — cosine between parent concept vector and child-minus-parent difference vectors over ~900 WordNet concepts; (b) simplex quality of categorical concepts; (c) linear-representation test statistics.
candidates.adds: Published, oral-at-ICLR replacement for BLME's custom geometry_categories (flagged in PAPERS.md as 'no canonical paper'), and the first unembedding-space feature-geometry task with a principled inner product — distinct from geometry_unembedding (effective rank only) and repe_concept_separability (activation-space, prompt-based). WordNet lemma lists ship with the repo — same label-light class as the WEAT word lists already accepted for consistency_bias_weat.
candidates.feasibility: Core computation needs only the unembedding matrix + tokenizer (weights-only, no forward passes for the main scores); runs on CPU in minutes for any model. Deps: torch, nltk/WordNet data (bundled word lists).
candidates.parity_feasible: Execute official notebooks 01/02 on Gemma-2B, pin the concept-vector cosine matrices and orthogonality statistics; BLME kernel must reproduce them numerically (deterministic linear algebra given the same WordNet splits).

candidates.name: Entropy / confidence-regulation neurons (unembedding null-space neuron taxonomy) — RE-PROPOSAL of prior-survey watch item #14 with a NEW argument
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2024 (Stolfo, Wu, Gurnee, Belinkov, Song, Sachan, Nanda)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/bpwu1/confidence-regulation-neurons (verified: fetched; official NeurIPS 2024 code; entry points run_and_store_ablation_results.py, run_and_store_unigram_results.py, induction.py; Hydra configs; GPT-2/Pythia/LLaMA)
candidates.measures: Neuron-level taxonomy of confidence regulation: (a) entropy neurons — final-MLP neurons with high w_out norm whose output lies mostly in the unembedding null space (weights-only norm-ratio score via SVD of W_U), modulating entropy through the final LayerNorm; (b) token-frequency neurons — neurons whose ablation shifts the output distribution along the log-unigram-frequency direction; plus total-vs-direct entropy effect under mean ablation.
candidates.adds: The prior survey watch-listed this (#14) citing only MEDIUM-confidence 'code via authors' and overlap fears with prediction_entropy. New argument: (1) the official repo is now located and verified (bpwu1/confidence-regulation-neurons), clearing the reproducibility bar; (2) the identifying metric is a weights-only null-space projection ratio plus a mechanism-level ablation effect — neither is the output-entropy statistic prediction_entropy reports, and BLME has no neuron-level taxonomy task at all (sparsity is aggregate L0; knowledge_neurons is attribution to facts). Fills the monosemanticity/neuron-taxonomy slot of this lens without needing an SAE.
candidates.feasibility: SVD of the unembedding + forward passes with mean ablation on a small corpus; paper itself runs GPT-2 small through LLaMA-7B, so small-LLM scale is native. Deps: torch, transformer-lens-style hooks, Hydra (only for the reference run).
candidates.parity_feasible: Run the official ablation scripts on GPT-2 small with fixed config; pin the identified entropy-neuron indices, their null-space norm ratios, and per-neuron entropy deltas; BLME must match indices exactly and values numerically.

candidates.name: Sparse feature circuits (SAE-feature-level circuit faithfulness/completeness)
candidates.venue: ICLR 2025 Oral (Marks, Rager, Michaud, Belinkov, Bau, Mueller)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/saprmarks/feature-circuits (verified: fetched; official; scripts/get_circuit.sh, scripts/evaluate_circuit.sh, experiments/faithfulness.ipynb; downloads pretrained Pythia-70M dictionaries — no SAE training required)
candidates.measures: Circuits over pretrained-SAE features discovered with integrated-gradients attribution. Model-level scalars: feature-circuit faithfulness F(C) and completeness as functions of node threshold, and circuit size/sparsity at fixed faithfulness — i.e., how well the model's behavior decomposes into a sparse set of interpretable features.
candidates.adds: Directly fills the 'SAE-based circuit metrics' half of this lens: BLME's causality_circuit_quality (ACDC) and causality_edge_attribution (EAP) operate on polysemantic components (heads/edges); no existing task measures circuit structure at feature resolution. Uses templated subject-verb-agreement data generated by the repo — no external benchmark labels; pretrained dictionaries are downloaded, satisfying the no-training constraint. Model coverage is limited to models with public SAEs (Pythia-70M, Gemma-2 via Gemma Scope) — the same accepted restriction as the existing interpretability_sae_features (GPT-2-only).
candidates.feasibility: nnsight + torch; Pythia-70M-scale circuits run in minutes on one GPU; heavier than closed-form tasks but far lighter than ACDC search since attribution is gradient-based.
candidates.parity_feasible: Run scripts/get_circuit.sh + scripts/evaluate_circuit.sh with the released Pythia-70M dictionaries and fixed thresholds; pin node/edge effect values and the faithfulness/completeness curve points; BLME must reproduce them numerically.

candidates.name: Transcoder circuits (MLP transcoder fidelity + input-independent circuit attribution)

candidates.name: Copy suppression score (negative/anti-copy head class)
candidates.venue: BlackboxNLP @ EMNLP 2024 (ACL Anthology 2024.blackboxnlp-1.22); McDougall, Conmy, Rushing, McGrath, Nanda
candidates.repo: https://github.com/callummcdougall/SERI-MATS-2023-Streamlit-pages (verified: fetched; official — README carries the paper citation and contains the cspa/ directory implementing copy-suppression-preserving ablation; research-grade fork of TransformerLens with a 'TODO: clean up' note)
candidates.measures: Per-head copy-suppression: (a) weights-only score — negativity of the OV circuit's action on the attended token's own logit (diagonal of W_U^T W_OV E projected through the unembedding); (b) CSPA — fraction of a head's effect preserved when only its copy-suppression behavior is kept (76.9% for GPT-2 small L10H7).
candidates.adds: Completes the head-role taxonomy with the negative-head class: interpretability_head_roles' previous-token/duplicate-token/induction scores are all positive-copy detectors, and no existing task detects heads that systematically suppress predicted-and-present tokens (the mechanism behind self-repair and calibration effects). The weights-only anti-copy diagonal is architecture-generic and closed-form.
candidates.feasibility: Core weights-only score: one pass over embedding/OV/unembedding matrices, cheap on CPU for small models. Full CSPA needs forward passes with projection ablations — heavier but GPT-2-small-scale in the reference.
candidates.parity_feasible: Weakest parity story of the eight (ranked last for that reason): the official repo is a messy TransformerLens fork, but the cspa/ code runs, and the paper pins hard numbers (L10H7 negative-diagonal stats, 76.9% CSPA on GPT-2 small) to match against; pin the OV-diagonal tensor from the repo's utils on fixed weights and the CSPA scalar for L10H7.

candidates.name: WeightWatcher official layer-quality metrics (HTSR alpha via PL-MLE, alpha_hat, rand_distance / correlation traps, num_spikes; SETOL ERG)
candidates.arxiv: 1810.01075 (primary, Martin & Mahoney; fetched OK); SETOL 2507.17912 (fetched OK); single-checkpoint anti-grokking evidence 2602.02859 (fetched OK)
candidates.venue: JMLR 22(165) 2021 lineage + Nature Comms 12:4122; SETOL arXiv 2025; anti-grokking arXiv 2026
candidates.repo: https://github.com/CalculatedContent/WeightWatcher (pip `weightwatcher` v0.8.0, 1.4k commits, maintained; SETOL experiments: github.com/charlesmartin14/SETOL_experiments)
candidates.measures: Per-layer weight-matrix ESD diagnostics from weights alone, zero data: power-law exponent alpha via the published PL/TPL MLE fit with KS-optimal x_min; alpha_hat = alpha-weighted log spectral norm (the Nature-Comms quality predictor); rand_distance = distance between the layer ESD and its randomized counterpart; num_spikes / correlation traps = eigenvalues beyond the MP bulk of the randomized matrix; mp_softrank.
candidates.adds: RE-PROPOSAL OF A 'NO-GAP' AXIS WITH A GENUINELY NEW ARGUMENT (survey item (c) said weight-space spectral is covered): (1) BLME's geometry_spectral alpha is a Hill estimator on singular values whose own docstring admits it is only a monotone transform (~2*alpha_MM - 1) of the published WeightWatcher alpha — so BLME currently CANNOT pass the official-code parity bar on its flagship weight metric; (2) alpha_hat, rand_distance and correlation-trap counts are distinct signals implemented nowhere in BLME (mp_bulk_deviation deviates ESD from analytic MP, not from the layer's own randomization — different null); (3) NEW 2026 evidence (Prakash & Martin, 2602.02859) shows alpha<2 + correlation traps detect memorization/anti-grokking at a SINGLE checkpoint with no train/test data — exactly the training-dynamics-free grokking/memorization signal this lens targets, which survey item (f) wrongly closed as 'needs checkpoints'.
candidates.feasibility: Weights-only, no forward passes at all; CPU SVDs; pip install weightwatcher (+powerlaw dep); minutes for <=7B models.
candidates.parity_feasible: Trivially: run weightwatcher.analyze() on pinned GPT-2/Pythia checkpoints and assert per-layer alpha, alpha_hat, rand_distance, num_spikes against BLME's implementation to numeric tolerance (or wrap the package directly, as BLME did for sae-lens). This simultaneously fixes the existing geometry_spectral parity debt noted in AUDIT_V2 section 5.

candidates.name: Local Learning Coefficient (LLC) — singularity-aware loss-landscape complexity via devinterp
candidates.arxiv: 2308.12108 (fetched OK); at-scale estimator 2402.03698 (resolves; devinterp docs implement it)
candidates.venue: arXiv stat.ML 2023 rev. 2024, widely cited (Timaeus developmental-interpretability program); estimator paper 2024
candidates.repo: https://github.com/timaeus-research/devinterp (official, pip `devinterp`, v2.0.1 released 2026-04, HuggingFace + TransformerLens support, Qwen2.5-0.5B quickstart)
candidates.measures: lambda-hat: the local learning coefficient at the trained checkpoint — the Singular-Learning-Theory effective dimensionality / degeneracy of the loss basin, estimated by SGLD sampling of the local tempered posterior over unlabeled-text LM loss. Refined per-module rLLC (arXiv:2410.02984) also available in-package.
candidates.adds: Genuinely new landscape quantity: dynamics_sharpness's Hessian trace/top-eigenvalue/SAM numbers are blind to degenerate (singular) directions, which dominate real LLM basins; LLC is the SLT-correct basin-complexity measure and is the standard grokking/phase-transition observable in the devinterp literature — usable here as a single-checkpoint complexity signal. No BLME task measures basin degeneracy/volume. Not in the prior survey.
candidates.feasibility: pip devinterp + torch; SGLD draws are forward+backward passes with transient weight perturbations (weights restored — no training/fine-tuning of the model); minutes-to-1h for 0.5B on one GPU; hyperparameters (nbeta, epsilon, gamma, chains, draws) must be pinned in config.
candidates.parity_feasible: Strong: devinterp ships quickstart notebooks with published LLC values for Qwen2.5-0.5B — pin seeds/hyperparams and match lambda-hat within sampling tolerance; plus exact-parity unit tests on their deep-linear-network / toy-potential examples where the true learning coefficient is known analytically.

candidates.name: Super weights — data-free localization of catastrophic scalar weights
candidates.repo: https://github.com/mengxiayu/LLMSuperWeight (official; analyze.py/evaluate.py, scripts reproducing all paper tables, published index of super-weight coordinates per model)
candidates.measures: Data-free, single-forward-pass detection of 'super weights': individual scalar parameters in early down_proj layers (located via spikes in down_proj input/output activations) whose zeroing raises perplexity ~3 orders of magnitude; metrics: super-weight count + coordinates, super-weight magnitude, super-activation magnitude, PPL-ratio-on-zeroing (causal criticality).
candidates.adds: Weight-space CAUSE of massive activations: interpretability_activation_sinks (Sun 2024 / Gu 2025 / Arroyo 2025) measures only the activation side; no BLME task ties model quality to identifiable scalar weights. Gives a weight-criticality / quantization-fragility scalar in the 'weight statistics predicting quality' lens, complementary to activation kurtosis. Not in the prior survey.
candidates.feasibility: One forward pass with hooks + a few PPL evaluations; trivial runtime on any small LLM; repo covers OLMo-1B/7B, Mistral-7B, Phi-3, Llama-7B–30B.
candidates.parity_feasible: Excellent: the repo publishes exact super-weight coordinates for common checkpoints — assert BLME's detector returns identical (layer, row, col) coordinates, and match the PPL-ratio numbers from their evaluate.py scripts.

candidates.name: Blockwise Hessian spectrum + block-heterogeneity (SLQ)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/zyushun/hessian-spectrum (official; blockwise & full Hessian ESD via stochastic Lanczos quadrature, includes GPT-2/openwebtext setup)
candidates.measures: Full and per-parameter-block Hessian empirical spectral densities via stochastic Lanczos quadrature on the LM loss (unlabeled text), plus a 'block heterogeneity' summary — dispersion/divergence of Hessian spectra across embedding/attention/MLP blocks (the paper's signature transformer landscape property that explains Adam-vs-SGD gap).
candidates.adds: HONEST OVERLAP FLAG: same Hessian family as dynamics_sharpness — but that task computes only scalar trace/top-1 eigenvalue on the LAST block plus SAM delta; the full ESD via SLQ and, especially, the cross-block heterogeneity scalar are structurally new landscape signals (curvature anisotropy across the architecture) that no BLME task captures. Add only if the family-refinement is judged worth it; the heterogeneity scalar is the new signal.
candidates.feasibility: Needs Hessian-vector products (backward passes); flash-attention must be disabled and forward/backward determinism enforced; GPT-2-scale on one GPU is fine; heaviest candidate on this list — restrict to a subset of blocks and small Lanczos order.
candidates.parity_feasible: Run their SLQ code as-is on GPT-2 with pinned seeds/batches and compare estimated spectral density grids / moments per block; then extract the SLQ kernel into BLME (same kernel-extraction pattern used for attribution/correlation-dimension in Campaign 2).

candidates.name: Filter-normalized loss-landscape sections (scale-invariant sharpness)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/tomgoldstein/loss-landscape (official PyTorch implementation; 1D/2D sections along filter-normalized random directions)
candidates.measures: LM loss evaluated along filter-normalized random directions in weight space around the checkpoint: 1D/2D landscape sections yielding scale-invariant sharpness/roughness scalars (loss rise at fixed normalized radius, width of the low-loss basin, section convexity). Filter normalization removes the parameter-rescaling ambiguity that makes raw sharpness numbers incomparable across models.
candidates.adds: HONEST OVERLAP FLAG: same family as dynamics_sharpness, but every existing BLME sharpness number (Hessian trace, top-eig, SAM delta) is parameter-scale-sensitive and hence not cross-architecture comparable — filter normalization is the canonical published fix, and it is FORWARD-ONLY (no gradients/Hessian). (NB: classic mode-connectivity proper needs two independently trained models, so that sub-axis of the lens is out of BLME's single-model mold; this is the single-model loss-landscape diagnostic that fits.)
candidates.feasibility: Forward passes at perturbed weight copies only; needs one in-memory weight clone; cheap at <=1B with a small eval batch; repo is PyTorch-0.4-era, so parity should target its direction-generation + normalization kernel rather than running it verbatim.
candidates.parity_feasible: Moderate: extract their filter-normalization / direction-sampling functions (net_plotter.py) with pinned RNG and assert identical normalized directions and identical 1D loss sections on a small reference net; the loss evaluation itself is standard cross-entropy so end-to-end numbers pin exactly given seed + batch.

candidates.name: Rate-distortion weight complexity (grokking compressibility)
candidates.repo: https://github.com/brantondemoss/GrokkingComplexity (official; main.py bayes_optimize_svd_quantization is the reference kernel)
candidates.measures: Intrinsic Kolmogorov-style complexity of a single checkpoint via principled lossy compression: Bayes-optimized coarse-graining (weight quantization + low-rank SVD truncation, subject to a loss-distortion budget measured with forward passes on data) followed by entropy coding — bits required to describe the network at fixed capability. High description length at fixed loss indexes the memorization regime; complexity falls upon generalization/grokking.
candidates.adds: No BLME task measures description length / compressibility of the weights (spectral alpha is a correlational shape statistic, schatten/rankme are rank statistics — neither is an operational bits measure). Fills the grokking/memorization axis of this lens with a single-checkpoint, label-free scalar (the paper tracks it over training, but the measure itself is defined per checkpoint). Not in the prior survey; survey item (f) only rejected checkpoint-trajectory progress measures.
candidates.feasibility: Research-grade uncleaned code (authors say so); the coarse-graining search needs repeated forward-pass loss evaluations; fine for <=1B models; deps torch + entropy coder; medium engineering effort to port.
candidates.parity_feasible: Moderate: run bayes_optimize_svd_quantization on their released modular-arithmetic transformer setup with pinned seeds and match the complexity estimates; then port the kernel to BLME and guard with a fixed-checkpoint regression test. Weakest code-maturity on this list — hold to kernel-level parity.

candidates.name: Input-loss-curvature memorization score
candidates.arxiv: 2402.18726 (fetched OK; ICML 2024 per dblp) + origin 2307.05831 (fetched OK)
candidates.venue: ICML 2024 (Ravikumar, Soufleri, Hashemi, Roy); origin paper ICML 2024 Spotlight
candidates.repo: https://github.com/DeepakTatachar/Privacy-Memorization-Curvature (official ICML 2024 implementation; companion github.com/purdue-nrl/Memorization-Curvature also official)
candidates.measures: Per-sample trace of the Hessian of the loss w.r.t. the INPUT (Hutchinson estimator) at the trained checkpoint — provably linked to memorization (Feldman score) and differential privacy, ~3 orders of magnitude cheaper than direct memorization estimation; BLME scalar = distribution summaries (mean, tail mass) of input-curvature over an unlabeled text sample, using LM loss w.r.t. input embeddings.
candidates.adds: A curvature-based, membership-ground-truth-free memorization propensity signal — geometrically orthogonal to consistency_membership_inference / consistency_contamination (which threshold log-prob scores) and to dynamics_sharpness (weight-space, not input-space, curvature). Fills the 'memorization signal' slot of this lens with landscape geometry. CAVEATS: origin paper epoch-averages curvature during training — the usable BLME variant is the single-checkpoint score from the ICML-2024 privacy paper; official code is vision (CIFAR/ImageNet), so the LLM port (curvature w.r.t. input embeddings) is an extension beyond the reference experiments; needs light backward passes.
candidates.feasibility: Hutchinson probes = a few gradient computations w.r.t. input embeddings per sample (input dim small, cheap); any small LLM; minutes. Deps: torch only.
candidates.parity_feasible: Kernel-level only: reproduce their per-sample curvature scores on their released vision checkpoints with their calc_curv scripts, assert BLME's Hutchinson kernel matches exactly, then apply to LLM embeddings with the extension explicitly documented (same 'kernel parity + documented extension' pattern BLME used where official code targets another modality).

BLME restores the whole span [1:, s:e] per layer (tracing.py:342-350) and gates on corruption-hurt (line 328). But Guo Eq. 3 defines ECE for arbitrary M ("we group predictions into M interval bins") — 15 was his experimental setting, not the metric definition. result.summary: The guard layer is genuinely strong: registry/metadata/docs completeness for all 82 tasks is enforced (EXPECTED_TASKS has 82 unique names, exact-count assert, bidirectional certification-metadata coverage, banned-string docs-drift guards; 92 guard tests pass in 0.11s), fixtures are checked-in JSON resolved via __file__, and collection of all 1293 tests is clean on this machine. But the suite does NOT survive a fresh clone: an unguarded module-level `from vendi_score import vendi` aborts the entire pytest run at collection (vendi_score is in no extras group and not installed by CI), so the GitHub Actions test workflow fails on the happy path; the py3.9 matrix job is additionally broken by a PEP 604 annotation in positional_decay.py. Three parity tests hardcode a previous Claude session's /tmp scratchpad reference-repo clones and silently skip everywhere else, and the ~13 importorskip-gated parity dependencies are undeclared, so CI green (once fixed) would still silently skip most of the advertised official-code parity suite. Secondary issues: docs guards are cwd-dependent (the banned-strings guard passes vacuously when run outside repo root), ~30 unguarded gpt2 from_pretrained calls fail instead of skip offline while one test permanently sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 mid-suite, and there is no [tool.pytest] config at all.

findings.title: Python 3.9 claimed (requires-python, CI matrix) but task registration crashes on 3.9
findings.evidence: `def _row_distance_correlation(attn_row: np.ndarray) -> float | None:` with no `from __future__ import annotations` (verified: only PEP 604 union in package lacking it). geometry/__init__.py:17 imports it, so `_register_all_tasks()` → TypeError on py3.9; tests/test_completeness.py:10 calls it at import time, so the 3.9 CI matrix job (test.yml:14) dies at collection. CI's import-check step misses it (blme.core doesn't import tasks).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `from __future__ import annotations` to positional_decay.py (or use Optional[float]); add a 3.9 smoke check that runs `_register_all_tasks()`, or drop 3.9 from requires-python and the matrix.

findings.title: Official-reference parity tests depend on a prior Claude session's /tmp scratchpad clones; skip silently everywhere else
findings.evidence: Hardcoded "/tmp/claude-1736197890/.../42dc090a.../scratchpad/refrepos/lipEstimation" (lipschitz:49-50), magnipy (test_magnitude_parity.py:61-62), GPTID (test_phd_dimension_parity.py:49-50 — no env-var override at all). 17 reference repos live only in that volatile /tmp dir; on any other machine (or after tmp cleanup) these tests skip, so the vs-official-code comparisons are never enforced in CI or for contributors.

findings.evidence: importorskip-gated packages across tests: rsatoolbox, pyhessian, nolds, captum, IsoScore, gudhi, persim, skdim, torchmetrics, networkx, ripser, nltk (enumerated via grep) — none in any extras group; `all` covers only runtime deps. CI installs `.[dev]` + scikit-learn (test.yml:26-29). Locally tests/tasks/parity gives "233 passed"; in CI those tests skip, so green CI does not mean the parity claims (VERIFICATION_LEDGER) were checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `test` extras group with the full parity dependency list, install it in test.yml, and consider `-W error` plus a max-allowed-skips check so silent skip regressions are visible.

findings.title: Docs-drift guard passes vacuously when pytest runs from any cwd other than repo root
findings.evidence: `DOCS = Path("docs")` is cwd-relative; `_docs_text()` joins glob results, so empty glob → "" → zero banned strings → pass. Demonstrated: `cd tests && pytest test_publication_docs.py ...` → test_no_stale_publication_identifiers PASSED while test_reference_repo_docs_are_conservative, test_completeness.py:159, and test_packaging.py:7 raise FileNotFoundError (3 failed, 1 passed).
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve repo root via `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` in test_publication_docs.py, test_completeness.py:159, and test_packaging.py:7, and assert the globbed doc list is non-empty before scanning.

findings.title: Offline behavior inconsistent: ~30 unguarded gpt2 downloads fail instead of skip, and one test permanently sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 mid-suite
findings.evidence: Module docstring (lines 10-11) claims cached-model tests skip offline, but only ~12 of ~45 `from_pretrained("gpt2")` sites are try/skip-guarded (AST scan: lines 539, 1011, 1240, 1357... UNGUARDED; also tests/test_common.py:70, tests/tasks/test_bias_task.py:24). Line 998 `os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")` has no teardown, so later download-needing tests become order-dependent on cold-cache machines.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a shared session fixture that loads gpt2 once inside try/pytest.skip and use it everywhere; replace the os.environ mutation with monkeypatch.setenv so it is undone after the test.

findings.title: No pytest configuration at all; observed deprecation will break future collection
findings.evidence: No [tool.pytest.ini_options], pytest.ini, setup.cfg, or root conftest.py (verified absent) — no testpaths, markers, or filterwarnings. Collect run under simulated missing deps prints pytest warning: "In pytest 9.1 this warning will become an error by default" for importorskip-on-ImportError (test_sharpness_parity.py:44 pattern); CI installs unpinned pytest, so a routine pytest upgrade flips today's skips into collection errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Add [tool.pytest.ini_options] with testpaths=["tests"] and pass exc_type=ImportError to importorskip calls (or pin pytest<9.1 in the dev extra until fixed).

findings.title: test_bias_task.py injects src/ into sys.path, bypassing the installed package; CI has no pip/HF caching
findings.evidence: Lines 15-16: `SRC = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "src"; sys.path.insert(0, str(SRC))` — unique among test files; can shadow the pip-installed blme and mask packaging bugs. Separately, test.yml has no actions/cache for pip or ~/.cache/huggingface, so each of the 4 matrix jobs re-downloads torch and gpt2 on every push.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the sys.path hack (the package is already importable via editable install); add pip and HF-hub cache steps to test.yml.

result.reasoning: Confirmed by reproduction: 3 legacy pairs with factual==exclusive on distilgpt2 yield {'mean_factual_prob': nan, 'mean_exclusive_prob': nan, 'mean_rejection_ratio': nan} — only a numpy "Mean of empty slice" RuntimeWarning, no error dict. common.py:220 "if not answer: return None" makes all triples skip; np.mean([]) at contrastive.py:128-130 is nan, inconsistent with line 94's {"error": "Need at least 1 sample"}. Confirmed. HF hidden_states[-1]==ln_f(block output): diff 0.0; vs raw block output 370.214 — matches cited evidence. Official kmeng01/rome patch_rep live-copies `h[1:, t] = h[0, t]` on transformer.h.{num} (raw output); tracing.py:356 instead patches cached post-ln_f state at the last layer, which gets ln_f'd twice. Reproduced on gpt2 subject-at-end: layers 0–10 match ROME exactly (diff 0.0), layer 11 diverges (−0.000227 vs +0.000006). Docstring claims to "match the ROME reference" — not a documented proxy. Finder's exact 0.121 magnitude didn't reproduce, but the defect stands.

findings.title: Tasks that fail via {"error": ...} returns are counted as completed; --strict passes and summary reports failed_tasks: 0
findings.evidence: Ran evaluate() with ripser/sae_lens missing: table shows 2 tasks '⚠ ERROR' ("Ripser library not installed"), yet SUMMARY: {"completed_tasks": 4, "failed_tasks": 0}, errors=null. fail_on_task_error (core.py:322) only inspects task_errors (exceptions), not error-dict results stored at core.py:286; results.py:98-99 counts them as completed.
findings.suggested_fix: In the task loop, treat results containing an 'error' key as failures: move them into task_errors (or add a warned_tasks count), so summary/errors/--strict/CI reflect them. Optional-dep failures should also name the extra to install.

findings.title: Documented max_memory model-arg is silently mangled: parse_model_args splits on every comma and drops fragments without '='
findings.evidence: python -c "parse_model_args('pretrained=gpt2,max_memory=0:20GiB,cpu:40GiB')" → {'pretrained': 'gpt2', 'max_memory': '0:20GiB'} — cpu:40GiB silently dropped, though wrapper.py:105 and docs/configuration.md:111 document exactly that syntax. Typos like 'dtype:bfloat16' are also silently ignored (returns {'pretrained': 'gpt2'}).
findings.suggested_fix: Support quoting/escaping (e.g. lm-eval style) or a dict-valued syntax for max_memory, and raise ValueError on fragments without '=' instead of silently skipping. Update docs/configuration.md and the wrapper docstring to match whatever is actually parseable.

findings.title: examples/demo.py prints 'Available tasks: []' and contains leftover dev comments

findings.title: results.json git_hash records the user's CWD repo, not BLME provenance

result.summary: Release-readiness review of the BLME harness. The happy path is solid: `pip wheel` builds a clean wheel (only blme code + assets/categories.json + tasks/configs/defaults.yaml + LICENSE; no stray files), `blme --help`/`list-tasks`/`list-tasks --json` (all 82 tasks with certification metadata), `--dry-run --strict` on both shipped recipes (default_all.yaml validates all 82 task names), and a real end-to-end run on distilgpt2 with 3 tasks (JSON and CSV output) all succeeded. Heavy deps (ripser/nltk/sae-lens/sklearn/lm-eval) are correctly optional: no top-level imports, registration of all 82 tasks works with them blocked, and missing-dep tasks degrade to clear per-task error messages without crashing the run. Code is Python-3.9-syntax clean and CI tests 3.9-3.12; __version__ is consistent via importlib.metadata. Main defects: (1) tasks that fail by returning {'error': ...} (including all missing-optional-dep failures) are counted as completed_tasks with failed_tasks=0, errors=null, and --strict does not trip — a silent failure mode for CI/programmatic use; (2) the documented max_memory model-arg is impossible to pass because parse_model_args splits on every comma and silently drops fragments without '=' (typos are also silently ignored); (3) the repo ships internal audit docs, LaTeX paper source (incl. neurips_2025.sty), and study results git-tracked in the harness repo, contrary to the project's own layout policy; (4) README's headline '74 diagnostic tasks' and its category table are stale vs the actual 82-task registry; plus a broken examples/demo.py first line ('Available tasks: []'), CWD-dependent git_hash provenance in results.json, and thin PyPI metadata/no py.typed.
