result.summary: Two identical evaluate() calls on distilgpt2 produce byte-identical results (verified), the results envelope records seed/git-hash/versions, and most geometry/causality tasks correctly use locally seeded generators. However, seeding relies on a single set_global_seed(42) at run start, so ~6 tasks that draw from the global torch/numpy RNGs (induction_heads, head_roles, sharpness, probing, superposition, and the sampling tasks by default) produce different feature values depending on which other tasks ran before them — empirically confirmed. Worse, the per-task `seed` config on the two sampling tasks is completely broken on the installed transformers 5.2.0: it passes an unsupported `generator=` kwarg to model.generate(), the resulting ValueError is swallowed, every prompt is skipped, and the task returns an error instead of metrics — so opting into reproducibility disables the task. Minor issues: several tasks reseed process-global RNGs mid-run (library pollution), and dtype/device/order sensitivity is undocumented.

findings.title: Setting the `seed` config on sampling tasks breaks them entirely on transformers 5.x (generator kwarg rejected, error swallowed)
findings.evidence: transformers 5.2.0 generate() raises ValueError for `generator=` ("model_kwargs are not used: ['generator']"); fallback at line 104 only catches TypeError, so line 111's broad except skips every prompt. Ran evaluate(distilgpt2, seed=0 in task_configs): task returns {"error": "No samples successfully generated"}; dynamics_generation_diversity.py:189-196 likewise returns {"error": "No completions generated"}.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not pass `generator` to generate(); instead call torch.manual_seed(seed) (saving/restoring RNG state) before each generate(), or catch ValueError in the fallback. Apply to both self_consistency.py and generation_diversity.py, and add a regression test that a seeded run yields metrics, not an error.

findings.title: Task results depend on which other tasks run in the same evaluate() call (global-RNG order dependence)
findings.evidence: Seeding is only set_global_seed(seed) at core.py:88; induction.py:122 draws torch.randint from the global RNG. Verified: evaluate(distilgpt2, seed=42, tasks=[induction_heads]) gives avg_induction_score=0.10347615, but tasks=[head_roles, induction_heads] gives 0.10295437 for the same task. Same pattern: head_roles.py:59-64, dynamics/sharpness.py:91/94 (Hutchinson vectors), interpretability/probing.py:82 and superposition.py:147 (global np.random.choice).
findings.suggested_fix: Use a per-task locally seeded generator (torch.Generator().manual_seed(cfg seed) / np.random.default_rng(seed)) as already done in geometry/lid.py, tracing.py, ablation.py; pass the run seed into task configs so each task is reproducible standalone and in any suite composition.

findings.title: Sampling tasks are unseeded by default (seed: None), so their metrics are only reproducible via incidental global-RNG state
findings.evidence: self_consistency.py:57 and generation_diversity.py:149 default `seed = self.config.get("seed", None)`; configs/defaults.yaml has no seed entry for either task (only vendi/phd have one). With seed=None, do_sample=True generation consumes the global torch RNG, so results inherit the order-dependence above — and the opt-in seed path is the broken one (finding 1).
findings.suggested_fix: Give both tasks a default seed in configs/defaults.yaml (e.g. seed: 42) once the seeded path is fixed, so default runs are self-contained reproducible.

findings.title: Tasks and evaluate() reseed process-global RNGs (library side effect / mid-run pollution)
findings.evidence: categories.py:145/285/369 and dynamics/stability.py:83 call np.random.seed(42); self_consistency.py:72/109 calls torch.manual_seed(seed); core.py:88 evaluate() itself calls set_global_seed (utils.py:24-26), silently reseeding random/numpy/torch of any host application embedding blme. Contrast with weight_activation_alignment.py:87-96, which correctly saves/restores torch RNG state around its seeded svd_lowrank.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace np.random.seed + np.random.choice with np.random.default_rng(seed) locals (pattern already used in lid.py/rmt_bulk.py); in library entry points either document the global reseed or save/restore RNG state around the run.

findings.title: No documentation of reproducibility guarantees or dtype/device sensitivity of feature values
findings.evidence: README's only reproducibility mention is the results envelope (line 105); docs/configuration.md never mentions `seed` despite `blme evaluate --seed` existing (cli.py:85). Nothing warns that feature values differ across dtype (fp16/bf16/fp32 — wrapper.py defaults to dtype=auto, so the same command gives different numbers per checkpoint dtype), across CPU/GPU, or that some tasks are suite-order dependent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Reproducibility' section to README/docs: what --seed covers, that exact values are dtype/device/library-version dependent (envelope records versions), and recommend pinning dtype=float32 for cross-machine comparisons.

result.summary: The core loop is largely well-engineered: error isolation works (verified end-to-end with a crashing task), signal-handler safety is explicitly handled (main-thread + SIGALRM checks, handler restore in finally), all 8 hook-registering tasks remove hooks in finally, and task registration has no fragile optional imports. However, four MAJOR issues remain: the per-task timeout is silently defeated by tasks' own broad except-Exception handlers (verified: a 2s-timeout task ran 10s and reported OK); the default corpus is loaded (200 samples) before per-task num_samples are resolved, so larger requests are silently capped while the envelope records the un-capped number (verified); the shared cache unconditionally stores full-vocab logits (~20 GB host RAM at 200x512 tokens for a 50k vocab) even when no logits-consuming task runs; and mixed diagnostic+lm_eval runs hold two model copies plus the cache in memory simultaneously. Several MINOR issues affect the results envelope (print-before-save ordering, non-strict JSON Infinity/NaN, cwd-dependent git hash, inconsistent summary counts).

findings.title: Per-task timeout silently defeated by task-internal broad exception handlers; timed-out task reported as OK
findings.evidence: Verified: task with config timeout=2 wrapping work in `except Exception: continue` ran 10.0s and printed '✓ OK slept=10', errors=None. SIGALRM fires once; _timeout_handler raises TimeoutError (an Exception), swallowed by any of the 55 `except Exception` blocks in src/blme/tasks/ (e.g. geometry/perplexity.py:107), then no alarm remains — task runs unbounded and is recorded as success.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the handler raise a custom class deriving from BaseException (e.g. class TaskTimeout(BaseException)) so task-level `except Exception` cannot swallow it, and catch TaskTimeout in the core loop. Also guard `signal.alarm(int(timeout_sec))` against int() truncating 0<timeout<1 to 0, which disarms the alarm entirely.

findings.title: Default corpus loaded before task configs are resolved: num_samples > 200 silently capped at 200 while envelope records the un-capped value
findings.evidence: Verified by run: evaluate(tasks=['geometry_svd'], task_configs={'geometry_svd': {'num_samples': 500}}) → corpus loader called with 200 (line 148 runs before the max-of-num_samples resolution at lines 230-237), log shows 'forward pass over 200 samples', yet envelope says cache_num_samples_resolved: 500. Results computed on 200 samples; metadata claims 500 — silent shortfall + wrong provenance.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve task configs and cache_num_samples first, then load the corpus with max(resolved cache_num_samples, max per-task num_samples, 200); or log a warning and write the actual sample count used into the envelope.

findings.title: Shared cache unconditionally stores full-vocab logits for every sample even when no logits-consuming task is in the run
findings.evidence: cache.py:377-379 appends outputs.logits for every sample ('always collected'); core.py:174-177 knows cache_logits_tasks={geometry_perplexity, consistency_calibration} but populate() (cache.py:67) has no need_logits flag. 200 samples x 512 tokens x 50257 vocab x 4B fp32 ≈ 20.6 GB host RAM for a hidden-state-only run (e.g. geometry_svd alone); Llama-3's 128k vocab ≈ 2.5x more.
findings.suggested_fix: Add need_logits to populate()/ModelOutputCache and only accumulate logits when a cache_logits_task is in the run; optionally store logits in fp16 or store per-position log-probs of the target token instead of full-vocab tensors.

findings.title: Mixed diagnostic + lm_eval runs hold two full model copies plus the cache in memory; pure-benchmark runs load the diagnostic model for nothing
findings.evidence: core.py:130 loads the model unconditionally (even when diagnostic_tasks is empty), then step 5 calls run_lm_eval → benchmarks.py:52 simple_evaluate(model='hf', model_args=...) loads a second copy while `model` and the populated `cache` remain referenced in evaluate()'s scope. Double GPU footprint → OOM for any model near half of VRAM; cache RAM also held throughout.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip load_model_and_tokenizer when diagnostic_tasks is empty; before the lm_eval phase, call cache.clear(), del model, gc.collect(), torch.cuda.empty_cache() (or pass the already-loaded HFLM instance into simple_evaluate).

findings.title: Results printed to terminal before being saved: any print failure destroys the whole run's results
findings.evidence: print_results_table (core.py:340) runs before save_results (core.py:343-344). It raises AttributeError if any task returns a non-dict (results.py:131 `"error" in result`, 169 `result.items()` — the ABC contract is not enforced), and prints ✓/⚠/✗ which raise UnicodeEncodeError on cp1252-redirected Windows output — where timeouts are already disabled, so Windows is a supported target. Hours of compute lost after all tasks succeeded.
findings.suggested_fix: Call save_results before print_results_table, and/or wrap the table print in try/except with an ASCII fallback for the status glyphs.

findings.title: results.json can contain bare Infinity/NaN — invalid strict JSON that breaks non-Python consumers
findings.evidence: json.dump(envelope, ..., default=str) uses allow_nan=True. Verified: json.dumps({'ppl': float('inf'), 'x': float('nan')}) emits `"ppl": Infinity, "x": NaN`. Tasks genuinely produce these (geometry/perplexity.py:110 returns float('inf') when cnt_total==0). JavaScript JSON.parse, Rust serde, and strict parsers reject the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Sanitize the envelope before dumping (replace non-finite floats with None or string sentinels) or pass allow_nan=False and handle the resulting ValueError with a sanitizing fallback.

findings.title: git_hash in the results envelope records the user's cwd repo, not the blme package version
findings.evidence: _get_git_hash runs `git rev-parse --short HEAD` with no cwd argument (results.py:33-38). A pip-installed blme executed inside any unrelated git repo stamps that repo's HEAD into the envelope as provenance — misleading reproducibility metadata; blme_version already covers the package.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass cwd=os.path.dirname(__file__) so the hash is only captured for editable/source installs of blme itself, and return None otherwise.

findings.title: Cache silently clamps out-of-range layer indices to the nearest valid layer
findings.evidence: get_hidden_states clamps: `actual = max(keys[0], min(actual, max_layer))` (cache.py:131-136). Requesting layer_idx=40 on a 6-layer model silently returns layer 5's hidden states; a config written for a larger model produces plausible-looking but wrong-layer metrics with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise ValueError (or at least logger.warning with the substituted layer) when the resolved index falls outside the cached key range instead of clamping silently.

findings.title: Envelope summary arithmetic is inconsistent: soft-error results count as completed, unknown tasks inflate total, lm_eval tasks collapse into one
findings.evidence: Verified run: tasks=[svd, crasher, bogus] → summary {"total_tasks": 3, "completed_tasks": 1, "failed_tasks": 1} — bogus is unaccounted; completed+failed≠total. Tasks returning {"error": ...} dicts (e.g. geometry/unembedding.py:64) count as completed_tasks while print_results_table shows them as '⚠ ERROR'. N lm_eval tasks become one '_lm_eval' result.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute completed as results without an 'error' key, add skipped_unknown and warned counts, and count lm_eval tasks individually so machine consumers can rely on completed+failed+warned+skipped == total.

findings.title: Duplicate task registration silently overwrites the earlier class
findings.evidence: register_task does `_TASK_REGISTRY[name] = cls` with no collision check (registry.py:8-10). A contributor adding a task whose name collides with an existing one silently shadows it; the run proceeds with the wrong implementation under a familiar name.
findings.suggested_fix: Warn (or raise unless cls is identical) when name is already registered.

findings.title: YAML recipes cannot set output_format; runner hardcodes JSON
findings.evidence: run_from_yaml reads output_dir, device, batch_size, limit, cache_num_samples, seed, task_timeout from the global section (runner.py:33-39) but never output_format, and does not pass it to evaluate() — CSV output is unreachable from the documented recipe path.
findings.suggested_fix: Read global.output_format (default 'json') and forward it to evaluate(output_format=...).

must_add.name: Under-trained ('glitch') token detection — Magikarp
must_add.rationale: EMNLP 2024 main (Outstanding Paper). Weights-only vocabulary-pathology axis none of the 82 tasks touches: geometry_tokenizer_efficiency is tokenizer-only fertility and geometry_unembedding is effective rank of W_U; neither detects per-token training-coverage failures. Zero forward passes, official repo publishes per-model reports in results/, so exact numeric parity (indicator values + top-N token IDs) is achievable. Cheapest, cleanest new signal in the batch.

must_add.name: Categorical & hierarchical concept geometry (causal inner product, Park et al.)
must_add.rationale: ICLR 2025 Oral + ICML 2024 MechInterp workshop Best Paper; independently proposed by two lenses (deduped here). Hierarchy-as-orthogonality and simplex-regularity under the whitened (causal) unembedding metric is a concept-structure signal distinct from geometry_unembedding (rank only) and repe_concept_separability (activation-space), and it gives BLME's custom geometry_categories a canonical published anchor. WordNet word lists ship in the repo — same label-light standard as consistency_bias_weat. Repo confirmed: numbered notebooks computing concept vectors, orthogonality tests, polytope validation on Gemma-2B/LLaMA-3-8B; deterministic linear algebra makes parity straightforward.

must_add.name: Norm-based attention analysis (||alpha f(x)||, Kobayashi et al.)
must_add.rationale: EMNLP 2020 canonical correction (~700+ citations) with EMNLP 2021 and ICLR 2024 follow-ups in the same official repo (confirmed: three per-paper directories). Every existing BLME attention statistic is raw-weight based; this shows raw alpha systematically overweights special tokens and separates true attention sinks from value-norm-cancelled ones, directly complementing interpretability_activation_sinks. Single forward pass, closed-form, no new dependencies; official notebooks pin exact tensors for elementwise parity (same pattern as the existing attention_rollout test).

must_add.name: Retrieval heads (per-head retrieval-score taxonomy)
must_add.rationale: New head-taxonomy class missing from interpretability_head_roles: cross-context copy-during-decode (the documented mechanism behind long-context factuality), vs the existing short-range previous-token/duplicate/induction scores. Fully label-light (synthetic needle/haystack), generation is explicitly in-mold. Repo confirmed: retrieval_head_detection.py emits per-head head_score JSON ({layer-head: scores}) for Llama/Yi/Qwen/Mistral/Phi-3 — a deterministic count ratio, so exact parity on pinned needle positions. Note: arXiv page shows preprint; ICLR 2025 acceptance is per the scout's proceedings check.

must_add.name: Sharded rank comparison test (provable benchmark contamination)
must_add.rationale: ICLR 2024 Oral (Hashimoto lab). Genuinely different signal from consistency_contamination's per-document Min-K% thresholding: a set-level exchangeability hypothesis test with exact false-positive guarantees ('is THIS benchmark in the training set', with a p-value). Repo confirmed: compute_sharded_comparison_test.py, canonical test files for 8 benchmarks, and deliberately contaminated models — a built-in positive control that makes the parity test unusually strong.

must_add.name: WeightWatcher official layer-quality metrics (alpha via PL-MLE, alpha_hat, rand_distance, num_spikes)
must_add.rationale: Re-raise of the prior survey's 'weight-spectral: no gap' verdict, accepted on a new argument I verified locally: src/blme/tasks/geometry/spectral.py's own docstring admits its Hill-estimator alpha is only a monotone transform of the published WeightWatcher alpha — i.e., BLME's flagship weight metric cannot pass the official-code parity bar today (matches the AUDIT_V2 parity-debt concern). alpha_hat, rand_distance, and correlation-trap/num_spikes use a randomized-layer null distinct from geometry_mp_bulk_deviation's analytic MP null and exist nowhere in BLME. Repo confirmed: pip weightwatcher v0.8.0, analyze() computes all listed metrics; weights-only, CPU, trivial parity (wrap or pin against the package). Adding this simultaneously fixes existing debt and adds new signals.

nice_to_have.name: Min-K%++ (calibrated pretraining-data detection)
nice_to_have.rationale: ICLR 2025 Spotlight; I fully verified arXiv + repo (official, includes all baselines). Kept out of must_add only because it refines the statistic of the existing consistency_contamination task (vocabulary-normalized z-score / mode test) rather than opening a new axis. Trivial parity; first candidate to promote if a must_add slot frees up.

nice_to_have.name: LapEigvals (Laplacian eigenvalue spectrum of attention maps) — re-raise of prior-survey #11
nice_to_have.rationale: Prior survey watch-listed this solely for unconfirmed repo + label-dependence; both blockers now resolved (official repo, EMNLP 2025, label-free spectral core). Graph-Laplacian spectra of attention are a different operator from all existing attention tasks.

nice_to_have.name: Transformer block coupling (Jacobian singular-vector alignment)
nice_to_have.rationale: ICLR 2025; first derivative-level spectral-geometry signal (nothing in the 82 examines block-Jacobian alignment) with a published capability correlation. Needs backward passes — acceptable under the dynamics_sharpness exemption; pip-installable official package makes parity clean.

nice_to_have.name: Representation Topology Divergence (RTD)
nice_to_have.rationale: ICML 2022; topological counterpart of the CKA layer-similarity family, sensitive to multi-scale cluster/loop changes CKA misses; distinct from topology_zigzag_persistence. Official pip-installable package; deterministic on fixed subsamples.

nice_to_have.name: Attention-map topological features (TDA4ATD)
nice_to_have.rationale: EMNLP 2021 oral; fills the biggest topology-lens hole — all 5 topology_* tasks consume hidden-state point clouds, none applies filtration-based topology to attention. Label-free feature core; golden-value parity on saved attention tensors.

nice_to_have.name: LLM-Check (single-pass attention-kernel + hidden-state log-det hallucination scores)
nice_to_have.rationale: The only verified single-forward-pass hallucination detector with official code — fills prior survey gap (a). Held out of must_add because it has no arXiv id (formally fails criterion 3) and its Hidden Score is adjacent to geometry_matrix_entropy; implement only the attention/hidden eigen-scores if adopted.

nice_to_have.name: Super weights (data-free single-parameter criticality)
nice_to_have.rationale: Proposed by two lenses (deduped). Weight-space localization + causal criticality is arguably distinct from interpretability_activation_sinks/kurtosis, and published coordinates make parity exact — but it is the closest-to-covered candidate (same phenomenon family as Sun 2024 massive activations) and the weakest venue (arXiv preprint). Committee call.

nice_to_have.name: POSIX (Prompt Sensitivity Index)
nice_to_have.rationale: Findings of EMNLP 2024, pip package, high parity. The axis is partially covered (consistency_format_robustness, consistency_paraphrase), but POSIX is the published likelihood-based index that would give those custom tasks a canonical anchor — similar upgrade logic to the Park paper vs geometry_categories.

nice_to_have.name: GRIDE scale-resolved intrinsic dimension + abstraction-phase onset
nice_to_have.rationale: ICLR 2025 with LLM-specific validation; adds the scale axis all five existing ID tasks lack, plus asymmetric information imbalance. Maintained pip dependency, easy float-tolerance parity vs dadapy.

nice_to_have.name: Density-peaks representation landscape (ADP clustering)
nice_to_have.rationale: NeurIPS 2024; density multimodality/hierarchy is orthogonal to all geometry and topology tasks (holes vs probability modes). Label-free core (peak counts/hierarchy); two-level parity via dadapy. Pairs naturally with GRIDE (shared dependency).

nice_to_have.name: Entropy / confidence-regulation neurons — re-raise of prior-survey #14
nice_to_have.rationale: Prior survey's two blockers (no located repo; overlap fear with prediction_entropy) are addressed: official NeurIPS 2024 repo now verified by the scout, and the weights-only null-space norm-ratio is not an output-entropy statistic. Would be BLME's first neuron-level taxonomy task.

nice_to_have.name: INSIDE / EigenScore — re-raise of prior-survey #9
nice_to_have.rationale: Legitimate re-raise: the old rejection ('needs sampling') no longer binds since generations are in-mold, and the prior survey's 'reduces to matrix_entropy' claim only covers the single-pass core, not the actual K-generation covariance. No auxiliary model needed, decoupled-generation parity pattern already used for coe.

nice_to_have.name: Sparse feature circuits (SAE-feature-level faithfulness/completeness)
nice_to_have.rationale: ICLR 2025 Oral; feature-resolution circuits genuinely absent (causality tasks operate on heads/edges). Accepted restriction: only models with public SAEs (same as interpretability_sae_features), which caps cross-model comparability — hence not must_add.

nice_to_have.name: SelfCheckGPT (SelfCheckNgram variant only)
nice_to_have.rationale: Canonical behavioral hallucination-consistency signal, not in the prior survey; n-gram variant is strictly single-model. Distinct from self_consistency (answer agreement) and generation_diversity. Deterministic scoring kernel gives clean parity.

nice_to_have.name: PriDe option-ID prior (MCQ selection bias)
nice_to_have.rationale: ICLR 2024 Spotlight; answer-choice-ID bias under content permutation is covered by no consistency task. Label-free PriDe prior kernel only (headline RStd needs labels — must be excluded and documented); modest extraction work from an experiment-shaped repo.

nice_to_have.name: Neural persistence + deep graph persistence (weight-space topology pair)
nice_to_have.rationale: Would be the only weights-only topological task. Adopt as a pair (DGP primary, NP sub-score) since TMLR 2023 shows classic NP is variance-dominated. TF1-era / Aleph-dependent reference code makes parity the main friction — Docker-pinned goldens.

nice_to_have.name: Euler characteristic curves & profiles (eulearning)
nice_to_have.rationale: JMLR 2024; fills the empty Euler-characteristic slot with all-degree topological information at near-linear cost; 2-parameter profiles beyond every 1-parameter topology task. Deterministic sklearn-style transformers, easy parity.

nice_to_have.name: Euclidicity / TARDIS singularity detection
nice_to_have.rationale: ICML 2023; measures where the manifold hypothesis fails — orthogonal to all four ID estimators that assume it. Python-version pin is the integration nuisance; vendor the kernel and pin goldens.

nice_to_have.name: Local Learning Coefficient via devinterp
nice_to_have.rationale: Proposed by two lenses (deduped). Basin degeneracy is provably distinct from dynamics_sharpness's curvature, and devinterp is maintained with a wrap-not-reimplement path (sae-lens precedent). Held back: hyperparameter-sensitive SGLD estimator, backward passes, no main-venue acceptance.

nice_to_have.name: MAUVE (human-likeness divergence frontier)
nice_to_have.rationale: NeurIPS 2021 Outstanding Paper; distributional human-likeness of open-ended generation is a real portfolio gap (all generation tasks measure internal diversity). Needs an unlabeled human reference corpus and a featurizer choice — pin both for parity.

nice_to_have.name: Text-diversity suite (compression ratio, self-repetition, templates)
nice_to_have.rationale: Cheap extension reusing dynamics_generation_diversity's completions; gzip compression ratio is an information-theoretic diversity signal distinct from n-gram counting. Maintained pip package, deterministic parity.

nice_to_have.name: Entropy calibration gap (generation entropy rate vs log loss)
nice_to_have.rationale: NeurIPS 2025; compares generative entropy rate to predictive log loss — the canonical degeneration/error-accumulation diagnostic, covered by no task. Decoupled-generation parity feasible.

nice_to_have.name: LLM-as-lossless-compressor (cross-modal compression rate)
nice_to_have.rationale: ICLR 2024; the cross-modal (text/image/audio bytes) compression profile and size-adjusted rate are new axes beyond geometry_perplexity. Arithmetic-coder kernel is pure Python with bit-identical parity; modality plumbing is the main effort.

nice_to_have.name: TOHA (topological divergence of attention during generation)
nice_to_have.rationale: ACL 2026; only generation-time topological signal. Requires the label-free adaptation (all-head distribution instead of the ~50-sample head selection) — an honest deviation from the reference pipeline, hence low rank despite good code.

nice_to_have.name: Transcoder circuits (MLP transcoder fidelity)
nice_to_have.rationale: NeurIPS 2024; transcoder slot is empty, but out-of-the-box coverage is GPT-2-small only (pretrained transcoders are model-specific), limiting cross-model comparability more than any accepted task.

nice_to_have.name: Information flow routes (llm-transparency-tool)
nice_to_have.rationale: EMNLP 2024; patching-free per-input circuit sparsity. Caveats: repo archived read-only and CC BY-NC (parity-oracle only, BLME reimplements); shares its norm-contribution kernel with the Kobayashi must_add — implement that first and reassess the marginal signal.

rejected_duplicates: Categorical/hierarchical concept geometry (second scout copy, lens 1) — identical method/arXiv/repo as the lens-3 proposal; merged into one must_add
Super weights (second scout copy) — two lenses proposed the same paper/repo; merged into one nice_to_have entry
Local Learning Coefficient / devinterp (second scout copy) — two lenses, same paper/package; merged into one nice_to_have entry
Domain-stratified BPC (2404.09937) — core quantity is BPC, already computed by geometry_perplexity; only the corpora/protocol are new (scout concedes)
Blockwise Hessian spectrum (2402.16788) — dynamics_sharpness family refinement, heaviest compute in the batch; heterogeneity scalar alone doesn't justify a new task
Filter-normalized loss sections (1712.09913) — another dynamics_sharpness-family refinement; 2018-era PyTorch reference weakens the parity story

Generating with Confidence / UQ-NLG EigV-Deg-Ecc (2305.19187) — same class as previously-rejected KLE; scout itself ranks it last of the three sampling-UQ candidates, redundant once INSIDE + SelfCheckGPT cover the family
Rate-distortion weight complexity (2412.09810) — authors call the code research-grade/uncleaned; fails BLME's official-code parity bar in practice
Input-loss-curvature memorization score (2402.18726) — official code is vision-only; the LLM variant is an undocumented extension beyond the reference experiments (kernel parity only)
Per/across-input diversity decomposition (2310.06452) — archived repo + external helper models; EAD-only subset is better handled as a revision of dynamics_generation_diversity than a new task
Copy suppression (2310.04625) — genuinely new head class but the scout concedes the weakest parity story (messy research fork); revisit if the head-taxonomy family is extended after retrieval heads
result.notes: Verification performed personally on all 6 must_add entries: arXiv abstract AND official repo fetched for each (12 fetches), all resolve and match the scouts' descriptions; additionally the WeightWatcher parity-debt claim was confirmed directly in src/blme/tasks/geometry/spectral.py (docstring lines 23-28 admit the Hill alpha is a monotone transform of published WW alpha). Nice_to_have entries were not independently re-fetched except Min-K%++ (verified both ends; it is must_add-grade and should be promoted first if a slot opens — held back only because it refines the existing consistency_contamination statistic rather than opening a new axis). One caveat on Retrieval Heads: the arXiv page lists no venue; ICLR 2025 acceptance rests on the scout's proceedings check. Prior-survey leftovers legitimately re-raised in this round: #11 attention-map spectral features (= LapEigvals; both original blockers now cleared), #14 confidence-regulation neurons (official repo now located), #9 EigenScore/INSIDE (the 'no generation' mold that justified rejection has been dropped from the criteria). Three prior-survey 'no gap / no add' verdicts are overturned by this batch: (a) single-pass hallucination — LLM-Check fills it with official code (blocked from must_add only by its missing arXiv id); (c) weight-space spectral 'covered' — contradicted by BLME's own geometry_spectral docstring (WeightWatcher must_add fixes it); (f) grokking 'needs checkpoints' — WW correlation-traps (arXiv:2602.02859) give a single-checkpoint memorization signal. One leftover NOT re-raised by any scout: Lookback-Lens (#12, watch) — still unaddressed if the RAG-context axis ever matters. Implementation note: if both the Kobayashi norm-attention must_add and info-flow routes are eventually adopted, implement the shared norm-contribution kernel once. Min-K%++, sharded test, and existing consistency_contamination together would form a coherent three-leg contamination family (doc score, calibrated doc score, set-level test).

result.reasoning: Reproduced on gpt2. hidden_states[12] == ln_f(raw last-block output) exactly (max diff 0; vs raw: 370.214), so tracing.py:356 patches a post-ln_f state into the block-output slot at the final layer. Subject-at-end prompt "The capital of Italy": shipped layer_11 AIE = 0.000384469 vs ROME semantics 0.121246044 (verified two ways: live row-0 copy and cached raw block output); layers 0-10 match exactly. result.summary: The model layer (src/blme/models/wrapper.py, ~220 lines, plus utils.py) is small and mostly sound for the plain-GPT2 path, but live testing against the installed transformers 5.2.0 exposed real breakage: attention-consuming tasks silently receive tuple-of-None attentions under the default SDPA load and two tasks (geometry_positional_decay, interpretability_attention_rollout) fail on the happy path because core.py's compensating force-eager list omits them; the documented multi-device max_memory syntax is unparseable by the comma-splitting arg parser; a missing/typo'd `pretrained` key silently benchmarks gpt2; and the quantization flags (load_in_8bit/4bit) hard-crash with TypeError on transformers v5, which the unbounded `transformers>=4.35.0` pin permits. Packaging omits accelerate/bitsandbytes needed by documented options, and set_global_seed omits cuDNN determinism settings. All findings were reproduced with actual runs (gpt2/distilgpt2, CPU).

findings.title: Attention tasks fail on default load: SDPA returns all-None attentions with no warning; force-eager list in core.py is incomplete
findings.evidence: Ran: default wrapper load (sdpa, transformers 5.2.0) gives outputs.attentions = tuple of 12 Nones, zero warnings. geometry_positional_decay -> misleading {'error': 'Could not compute positional correlations (sequences too short or nan).'}; interpretability_attention_rollout -> error dict. Both succeed with attn_implementation=eager. Neither task is in force_eager_tasks (core.py:190-196); positional_decay.py:84-85 silently skips None entries.
findings.suggested_fix: Add interpretability_attention_rollout and geometry_positional_decay to force_eager_tasks (or derive the set from task metadata instead of a hardcoded list). In positional_decay, detect all-None attentions and report the real cause. Consider having the wrapper log a warning when attn impl is sdpa/flash and the run needs attentions.

findings.title: Documented multi-device max_memory syntax is silently mangled by comma-splitting parser
findings.evidence: Docstring (wrapper.py:105) advertises max_memory='0:20GiB,cpu:40GiB', but parse_model_args splits the whole model_args string on ','. Ran: parse_model_args('pretrained=gpt2,max_memory=0:20GiB,cpu:40GiB,dtype=float16') -> {'pretrained':'gpt2','max_memory':'0:20GiB','dtype':'float16'}; 'cpu:40GiB' dropped with no error.
findings.suggested_fix: Either use a quoting/escaping scheme (e.g. semicolons inside max_memory: '0:20GiB;cpu:40GiB') or a smarter parser; at minimum raise on tokens without '=' instead of silently discarding them, and fix the docstring.

findings.title: Missing or typo'd 'pretrained' key silently evaluates gpt2 instead of erroring
findings.evidence: wrapper.py:116 args.get('pretrained', 'gpt2') plus parse_model_args silently ignoring unknown keys and '='-less tokens. Ran: load_model_and_tokenizer('pretrainedd=distilgpt2') loads and reports gpt2 — the user's entire evaluation runs on the wrong model with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Require 'pretrained' explicitly (raise if absent) and warn/raise on unrecognized model_args keys; keep gpt2 only as a CLI-level documented default if desired.

findings.title: load_in_8bit/load_in_4bit crash with TypeError under transformers v5, which the unbounded version pin allows
findings.evidence: pyproject pins transformers>=4.35.0 (no upper bound); installed 5.2.0. Ran: AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('distilgpt2', load_in_8bit=True) -> TypeError "GPT2LMHeadModel.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'load_in_8bit'". TypeError is not caught by _load_model's (ValueError, OSError) fallback (wrapper.py:216), so the documented flag hard-crashes.
findings.suggested_fix: Build a BitsAndBytesConfig and pass quantization_config= (works on 4.35+ and v5). Also switch torch_dtype= to dtype= (v5 prints '`torch_dtype` is deprecated! Use `dtype` instead!' on every load; wrapper.py:146-148) or gate on transformers version.

findings.title: accelerate (and bitsandbytes) not declared anywhere, but documented device_map/max_memory/quantization options require them
findings.evidence: Ran: load_model_and_tokenizer('pretrained=distilgpt2,load_in_8bit=true') -> ValueError "Using a `device_map`... requires `accelerate`. You can install it with `pip install accelerate`". Neither accelerate nor bitsandbytes appears in dependencies or any optional extra, yet wrapper.py:99-105 documents device_map, max_memory, load_in_8bit/4bit.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an extras group, e.g. [project.optional-dependencies] gpu = ['accelerate'] and quant = ['accelerate','bitsandbytes'], and mention it in the wrapper docstring/README.

findings.title: set_global_seed omits cuDNN/deterministic-algorithms settings, so GPU runs are not bit-reproducible
findings.evidence: utils.py:17-28 seeds random/numpy/torch/cuda only. No torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True, no torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False, no torch.use_deterministic_algorithms; core.py:87-88 relies solely on this for the run's reproducibility claim (seed recorded in results at core.py:333).
findings.suggested_fix: Add optional deterministic=True path setting cudnn.deterministic/benchmark and (best-effort) torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True); document that sampled-generation tasks are only reproducible on identical hardware/versions.

findings.title: Pad-token fallback silently leaves pad_token=None for tokenizers lacking both EOS and BOS
findings.evidence: wrapper.py:131-137: if eos_token is None the code assigns tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.bos_token; when bos is also None this is a silent no-op, and the comment 'critical for batched inputs' is violated — any later padded batch raises 'Asking to pad but the tokenizer does not have a padding token' far from the cause.
findings.suggested_fix: After the fallback chain, if pad_token is still None either add a pad token (tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'pad_token':'<|pad|>'}) + resize embeddings) or log a clear warning naming the model.

result.reasoning: Confirmed by execution. With prompt " ", gpt2/pythia/Qwen2.5/SmolLM2 tokenizers merge the space into the first token (ĠJohn, offset end 5 > pl=1) giving prompt_len=0; common.py:269 slices logits[-1:-1] (empty) → None. Running the task on gpt2 with bundled defaults returns {'error': 'No valid samples processed.'} while the conditional call succeeds (NLL 4.042). OPT's BOS </s> (offset (0,0)) gives prompt_len=1, so only BOS families work. No paper reference applies (docstring: in-house diagnostic). Genuine BUG, correctly classified.

result.summary: The suite is large and well-designed at its core: 1293 tests collect cleanly in 0.7s with zero import-time errors/warnings; conftest.py builds tiny random-weight models across 11 architectures with no downloads; the completeness/metadata guards genuinely enforce the 82-task catalog (exact count, instantiability, certification coverage in both directions), and most of the 31 official-code parity tests pin numbers in checked-in JSON fixtures rather than requiring live reference repos. However, GitHub Actions CI on main is currently FAILING (badge confirms), and I reproduced two concrete causes: an unguarded module-level `from vendi_score import vendi` (collection error — vendi_score is in no pyproject extra and not installed by test.yml) and two ripser-dependent tests that fail (one with a raw import, one via a NameError in blme product code) while CI installs only `.[dev]` + scikit-learn. Three parity tests hardcode another Claude session's ephemeral /tmp scratchpad as the reference-repo location (one with no env-var escape hatch), so their "official code parity" checks silently skip for everyone forever after a reboot. The suite also hard-requires HF Hub network on a fresh clone (unguarded gpt2 downloads; `dataset=None` paths that only catch ImportError around load_dataset), and the docs-drift guards use cwd-relative paths — the stale-identifier guard passes vacuously when pytest runs from any other directory. There is no [tool.pytest.ini_options] section at all. Fixture JSONs leak local machine paths in provenance fields.

findings.title: CI on main is red: test.yml dependency set cannot run the suite (vendi_score collection error, ripser test failures)
findings.evidence: Badge fetch: 'Tests - failing'. test.yml installs only `.[dev]` + scikit-learn. tests/tasks/parity/test_vendi_parity.py:36 has module-level `from vendi_score import vendi` (vendi_score in no extra) -> collection error. Simulated missing ripser: `2 failed, 33 passed` (tests/tasks/test_reference_parity_formulas.py:315 raw `from ripser import ripser`; test_topology.py betti test).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `test` extra (or extend dev) with scikit-learn, ripser, vendi_score, nltk, etc., and install it in CI; guard vendi_score with pytest.importorskip at module level and the ripser import at test_reference_parity_formulas.py:315 with importorskip. Make the badge green before release.

findings.title: Three parity tests hardcode an ephemeral Claude-session /tmp scratchpad as the official-reference location; phd has no override at all
findings.evidence: _REF_CANDIDATES contains only '/tmp/claude-1736197890/.../42dc090a-.../scratchpad/refrepos/GPTID' — no env var. test_lipschitz_parity.py:49 and test_magnitude_parity.py:61 same path with LIPESTIMATION_DIR/BLME_MAGNIPY_DIR fallbacks. /tmp is wiped on reboot, so these reference-parity tests silently skip forever, for maintainer and contributors alike.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the scratchpad paths; resolve references via documented env vars (add BLME_GPTID_DIR for phd) or a tests/refrepos/ convention documented in CONTRIBUTING, so 'official code parity' remains re-verifiable.

findings.title: blme product code crashes with NameError (not a clean error) when ripser is missing and _count_betti is reached
findings.evidence: Module guard sets HAS_RIPSER=False on ImportError (lines 40-44) but `_count_betti` calls bare `ripser(...)` at line 108. Reproduced: with ripser absent, tests/tasks/test_topology.py::test_betti_curve_geodesic_recovers_clusters_and_loops fails `NameError: name 'ripser' is not defined` at betti_curve.py:108 — a misleading crash instead of the intended 'pip install ripser' message.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise ImportError with the install hint inside _count_betti when HAS_RIPSER is False, and add pytest.importorskip('ripser') to the direct-helper test.

findings.title: Fresh-clone test run hard-requires HF Hub network; download failures surface as test failures, not skips
findings.evidence: GPT2TokenizerFast.from_pretrained('gpt2') at test_common.py:70,99 and tests/tasks/test_bias_task.py:24 are unguarded (contrast test_comprehensive_parity.py:48 which skips on cache miss). 54 tests pass dataset=None, triggering load_dataset('EleutherAI/lambada_openai') where only ImportError is caught (betti_curve.py:149 pattern), so offline/firewalled contributors get crashes.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap all from_pretrained/load_dataset calls in tests with the existing try/pytest.skip('not available offline') pattern, and catch OSError/ConnectionError (not just ImportError) in tasks' dataset-download fallbacks.

findings.title: Docs/packaging drift guards are cwd-relative; the stale-identifier guard passes vacuously when run from another directory
findings.evidence: Ran `cd /tmp && python -m pytest <abs paths>`: 3 failed (FileNotFoundError: 'docs/getting_started.md', REPOSITORIES.md, pyproject.toml), 1 passed — the passing one is test_no_stale_publication_identifiers, because `Path('docs').glob('*.md')` is empty so text=='' and no banned pattern matches: the guard silently asserts nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor with REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] in test_publication_docs.py, test_packaging.py:7, test_completeness.py:159, and assert the doc set is non-empty before scanning.

findings.title: No pytest configuration at all (no [tool.pytest.ini_options], pytest.ini, or markers)
findings.evidence: pyproject.toml has no [tool.pytest.ini_options]; no pytest.ini/setup.cfg/tox.ini exist. No testpaths (rootdir depends on invocation cwd, feeding the cwd-relative guard issue), no filterwarnings policy, no slow/network markers to let contributors deselect the gpt2-downloading parity tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Add [tool.pytest.ini_options] with testpaths=['tests'], registered markers (e.g. network, slow, reference), and use them to gate download-heavy tests (-m 'not network').

findings.title: Checked-in parity fixtures leak local machine and Claude-session paths in provenance fields
findings.evidence: grep shows 'venv': '/tmp/claude-1736197890/.../scratchpad/venvs/tlens2' in head_roles.json:7, induction_heads.json:7, spectral.json:16, edge_attribution.json:22, knowledge_neurons.json:7, and '/home/dtsaras/miniconda3/...' in correlation_dimension.json:13. Provenance references environments no one (including the maintainer, post-reboot) can inspect.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace machine-local paths with portable provenance: package name + version + upstream commit hash (already present in some fixtures).

findings.title: No guard that every registered task is documented in docs/tasks_*.md (currently satisfied but unenforced)
findings.evidence: Only docs guard is the literal string '82 diagnostic tasks' in getting_started.md. I scripted the real check: all 82 registered task names do appear somewhere in docs/*.md today ('not mentioned in docs: 0'), but nothing prevents a new task from shipping undocumented.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test iterating list_tasks() and asserting each name appears in the concatenated docs/tasks_*.md text.

result.reasoning: Confirmed. Live repro: load_dataset('coastalcph/mpararel','en') raises "ValueError BuilderConfig 'en' not found. Available: ['default']". HF datasets-server: sole config 'default'; features are id/language/relation/template/template_id/query/... — no 'relation_id' or 'text', so paraphrase.py:62 would KeyError anyway. except Exception (line 75) falls back to 5 _BUNDLED triples, logged only at logger.info. Branch is unreachable dead code, not a documented proxy; [BUG] classification is correct.

Confirmed. docs/PAPERS.md:317 says verbatim "add Kirichenko 2023 for paraphrase-invariance motivation"; no such paper exists (Kirichenko 2023 = spurious-correlations/last-layer retraining, not paraphrase invariance). The repo's own VERIFICATION_LEDGER.md:121 cites arXiv 2404.15206 (Fierro, Li, Søgaard 2024, "Does Instruction Tuning Make LLMs More Consistent?" — verified real), and paraphrase.py:58 loads coastalcph/mpararel from Fierro's group. Elazar 2021 ParaRel (arXiv 2102.01017) verified real. Suggested fix is correct; docs-only citation defect.

result.summary: The happy path is solid: `blme evaluate --model-args pretrained=distilgpt2 --tasks geometry_svd geometry_lid interpretability_attention_entropy --device cpu` ran end-to-end in ~5s with a correct results.json envelope (README's `effective_rank` key exists); `list-tasks`, `--json`, `--dry-run --strict`, and both example recipes validate; the built wheel is clean (101/101 py files, assets + defaults.yaml included, no stale build/ leakage, internal docs excluded); optional deps (ripser/nltk/sklearn/sae-lens/lm-eval/wandb) are all lazily imported with clear install-hint messages. Four real release defects: (1) the package crashes at import on Python 3.9 (advertised minimum, in CI matrix) due to a PEP 604 `float | None` runtime annotation; (2) tasks that fail by returning `{"error": ...}` (the standard path for missing optional deps) are counted as completed — `--strict` exits 0 and the JSON summary reports failed_tasks=0/errors=None, contradicting documented behavior; (3) the git repo ships a large amount of internal paper/audit material (paper/ with NeurIPS .sty and figures, root main.tex/references.bib, AUDIT_*.md, VERIFICATION_LEDGER.md, results/ study outputs); (4) the declared build minimum setuptools>=61 cannot actually build the project (verified failure on 75.9.1 due to the PEP 639 license string). Plus stale README task counts (74 vs actual 82), a demo script that prints an empty task list, no py.typed, and thin PyPI metadata.

findings.title: Package crashes on import under Python 3.9, the advertised minimum (requires-python >=3.9)
findings.evidence: `def _row_distance_correlation(attn_row: np.ndarray) -> float | None:` — PEP 604 union evaluated at def time; no `from __future__ import annotations`. Module is imported by geometry/__init__.py:17, which core._register_all_tasks (core.py:37) imports, so every CLI command and `import blme.core` raises TypeError on 3.9. Only occurrence (AST scan of all 101 files). CI matrix includes 3.9 (test.yml:14).
findings.suggested_fix: Change to `Optional[float]` or add `from __future__ import annotations` to positional_decay.py; alternatively bump requires-python to >=3.10 and drop 3.9 from the CI matrix and README badge.

findings.title: Task failures returned as {"error": ...} are silently counted as successes: --strict exits 0, summary says failed_tasks=0, errors=None
findings.evidence: Ran CLI with ripser blocked: `blme evaluate --tasks topology_homology --strict` → table shows '⚠ ERROR ... Ripser library not installed' but EXITCODE=0 and results.json has summary {'completed_tasks': 1, 'failed_tasks': 0}, errors: None. cli.py:102 promises --strict fails 'if any task errors'; core.py:322 only checks raised exceptions, and many tasks return error dicts (e.g. probing.py:100, homology.py:68).
findings.suggested_fix: In build_results_envelope and the strict check, treat results containing an 'error' key like task_errors: count them in failed_tasks, surface them in the errors field, and make fail_on_task_error raise. CI users piping results.json currently see clean success on broken runs.

findings.title: Internal paper/audit/study artifacts are git-tracked and will ship with the open-source repo
findings.evidence: `git ls-files` shows AUDIT_REPORT.md, AUDIT_V2.md, root main.tex + references.bib, REPRODUCE.md, RESEARCH.md, TASK_FIXES.md, VERIFICATION_LEDGER.md, full paper/ (main.tex, neurips_2025.sty, figure PDFs, tables), results/study_v1..v3 + audit outputs, docs/PAPERS.md, PAPER_SURVEY.md, TOP_PREDICTORS.md — study/paper material that per CLAUDE.md belongs in the other two repos. Wheel itself is clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Move paper/, results/, root main.tex/references.bib, and audit/verification markdowns to beyond_benchmarks / the paper repo before the public push (an uncommitted cleanup deleting scripts/ is already in flight in the working tree — extend it to these files). Note neurips_2025.sty redistribution and unpublished study results are also a leak concern.

findings.title: README headline task counts are stale: claims 74 tasks (27 geometry / 15 interp / 4 topology) but registry has 82 (32 / 17 / 5)
findings.evidence: `blme list-tasks` prints 'Available BLME tasks (82)'; per-group counts: geometry 32, interpretability 17, topology 5, causality 6, consistency 12, dynamics 6, repe 4. README.md:13-23 says 74 with the old per-category table; docs/getting_started.md:86 also says topology '(4 tasks)' (actual 5, so its categories sum to 81, not 82).
findings.suggested_fix: Update README table and getting_started.md counts to match the registry (82; topology=5 including zigzag). Consider a test asserting doc counts against len(list_tasks()) — tests/test_publication_docs.py exists and evidently doesn't cover README.

findings.title: Declared build-system minimum (setuptools>=61) cannot build the package: PEP 639 license string needs setuptools>=77
findings.evidence: pyproject has `license = "MIT"` (string) with `requires = ["setuptools>=61.0"]`. Verified: building with setuptools 75.9.1 fails — 'configuration error: `project.license` must be valid exactly by one definition ... BUILD FAILED: ValueError | invalid pyproject.toml config: `project.license`'. Works only because isolated builds fetch latest setuptools; pinned/offline/no-isolation builds break.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump to `requires = ["setuptools>=77.0.3"]` (or revert to `license = {text = "MIT"}` if 61 compatibility is desired).

findings.title: examples/demo.py prints 'Available tasks: []' and contains internal scaffolding comments
findings.evidence: Ran `python examples/demo.py`: first output line is 'Available tasks: []' because list_tasks() is called before any task registration (registration happens lazily inside evaluate()). File also ships comments '# Mock evaluation' and 'using mocked model loading for speed/test if possible' — leftover dev notes in the showcase example.
findings.suggested_fix: Call blme.core._register_all_tasks() (or expose a public registration hook) before list_tasks(), and delete the mock-related comments. Consider making list_tasks() self-registering since the CLI already has to work around this (cli.py:141-145).

findings.title: No py.typed marker despite fully type-hinted public API
findings.evidence: `find src -name py.typed` → nothing; wheel contains no py.typed and package-data (pyproject.toml:77-81) only lists assets/*.json and tasks/configs/*.yaml. Downstream mypy/pyright users get no types from `from blme import evaluate` even though core.py/base.py are annotated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add src/blme/py.typed and include it in [tool.setuptools.package-data] blme = ["py.typed", ...].

findings.title: Thin PyPI metadata: no Python-version or license classifiers, no keywords, only a Homepage URL
findings.evidence: Classifiers are only 'Programming Language :: Python :: 3' and 'Operating System :: OS Independent' (pyproject.toml:13-16); no 3.9–3.12 classifiers matching the CI matrix, no Repository/Issues/Documentation URLs, no keywords. Wheel METADATA confirms. Hurts PyPI discoverability and version filtering.
findings.suggested_fix: Add per-version classifiers (or trim to supported versions after fixing the 3.9 bug), 'License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License' or rely on License-Expression, keywords, and Repository/Issues entries under [project.urls].

findings.title: [data] extra is a no-op (datasets is already a core dependency)
findings.evidence: dependencies list includes `datasets` (pyproject.toml:36) while optional-dependencies keeps `data = ["datasets"]` with a back-compat comment; README (line 38) and getting_started.md (line 15) still advertise `pip install -e ".[data]"` as if it enabled functionality.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the [data] extra (or keep it but remove it from the docs' installation instructions) so users aren't led to believe dataset-backed tasks need an extra.
